Doctor Sophia, a 'Healthy Habits for Kids' channel built around a doctor character, gained about 651M US views in those 30 days, backing our own best performer (Lion Needs a Doctor) and the case for a recurring friendly doctor or helper in our songs.

Nursery rhyme channels keep scaling in the US: Lalafun (+654M views in 30 days), Toddler Zoo (+530M) and NuNu TV (+447M), alongside the bilingual Spanish English family music act 123 Andres (+868M), so both classic rhyme songs and bilingual music have big US demand.

Super Simple Songs reached 20 years in 2026 with over 70M subscribers and over 90B views; it began as teachers writing simple songs to help pupils learn English and now has a self funded Toronto studio of 40+ animators, musicians, puppeteers and educators.

Super Simple Songs now uploads about once a week, alternating a new song with a 'Top 20' themed compilation (counting, circle time, back to school, book songs), and its themed Top 20 mixes earn 1.1 to 3.5M views each, a steady compilation rhythm for a mature channel.

Super Simple's strongest new song of 2026 is an upbeat 'everybody celebrate' party song (6M views in under three months), ahead of a counting to 20 sea animals song made with another kids channel (3.1M) and a pack your bag trip song (2.7M): party, counting and adventure themes lead.

Lalafun (15.2M subs, 714 videos since Oct 2022) gains 600 to 700M views and 500 to 700K subscribers a month from about 15 uploads a month; its all time hits are classic rhymes with a twist: animal version Wheels on the Bus (955M), Five Little Ducks colours (726M), Old MacDonald safari (407M), counting 10 pandas (337M).

Lalafun runs local language channels (German, Indonesian, Arabic, Canada and US feeds), and its newest US video uses a mystery question title ('Where did the animals' colours go?'), the same curiosity hook that works for Shorts.

Super Simple Songs also partners with outside brands and channels for single songs (a hockey song with the NHL, a counting song with Noodle and Pals), a way big kids channels borrow each other's audiences.

Because classroom viewing runs through teachers, songs that work for circle time (a clear learning point, a calm teacher friendly title, no ads style hype) can reach children through lesson plans; Super Simple Songs was built exactly this way by teachers.

Bebefinn, Pinkfong's 3D baby and family song brand launched only in 2022, reported more than 80M subscribers and 58B views across its YouTube channels in Jun 2026 and about 84M and 65B by Aug 2026, the fastest climb of any new 3D kids song brand.

Pinkfong's first Amazon Kids+ original, The Big Book of Bebefinn (announced Jun 2026), is 18 musical episodes of about seven minutes following a toddler through everyday firsts such as riding a tricycle, visiting the doctor and trying new foods, mixing new songs with fan favourite hits.

La Granja de Zenon started in 2011 as preschool farm songs, and its named animal characters (a cow, a little rooster, a horse) grew bigger than the songs, so a small cast of recurring named animal friends around the Bros can become the brand kids ask for.

When CoComelon's main channel matured it grew through side character spin off channels: JJ's Animal Time reached 200M+ views a month (with its own animal songs and adventures spin offs), Cody Time 60M+ and Nina's Familia 40M+, so an animals themed Bro Bros playlist or sub series is the proven next step once the main channel has traction.

Little Angel's main English channel (7.3M subs, 2,278 videos) gained only 0 to 10K subscribers and 14 to 36M views in most months of 2026 (Aug spiked to 125M), so even a Moonbug brand's single channel plateaus without new formats; its Spanish, Portuguese and Indonesian channels carry much of the growth.

123 Andres, a Grammy and Latin Grammy winning bilingual Spanish English family music act, has 13.2M subscribers and 26.9B views from 3,013 videos, and its monthly views climbed from about 448M (Aug 2026) to 583M (Sep) and 797M (Oct), with new uploads reaching about 800K views in a day and a half.

In vidIQ's US ranking (Nov 2026) Toys and Colors has 123B lifetime views on 83M subscribers (about 1,480 views per subscriber) versus about 1,130 for CoComelon, and Filaretiki has about 1,220, so the channels kids replay most are simple, repeatable play formats rather than the biggest subscriber counts.

Pinkfong and Dr Seuss Enterprises made their first crossover on 16 Oct 2026: a Baby Shark Halloween remix plus a 'Guess Baby Shark's Halloween Costume!' sing along where viewers guess each costume, posted on both channels so each brand feeds the other's audience.

Dr Seuss Enterprises' relaunched YouTube channel reached 230.9M views and 2M subscribers in just over two years by turning classic characters into baby versions for nursery style songs, the same baby character trick CoComelon and Bebefinn use.

Disney bought Gracie's Corner, a family made YouTube sing along brand (6.3M subscribers, nearly 10B views) with original songs like a Good Morning Song, Veggie Dance and Play Outside, as a library of 120+ shorts and 18 themed compilations for Disney+ and Disney Jr. from 15 Jun 2026, with new originals to follow.

Disney Jr. itself makes short stop motion sing along music videos for each holiday (Mickey and Minnie's Holiday Songs: Halloween, then Christmas), so seasonal short sing along clips are a format even the biggest studio uses for preschoolers.

Peppa Pig revealed in 2026 that little brother George is moderately deaf (new season from 23 Mar, with short clips first on its YouTube channel), its second disabled character after wheelchair user Mandy Mouse, made with the National Deaf Children's Society and a deaf script consultant; disability is still rare in kids TV, so a natural inclusive friend in Bro Bros would stand out.

LooLoo Kids (62.7M subscribers, 43B views) titles almost every new upload as a medley of its recurring Johny character plus a classic rhyme ('Bath Song + Wheels on the Bus'), and its seasonal Halloween medleys reached 8 to 12M views within weeks in Oct 2026, so naming two familiar songs in one title widens Search reach.

LooLoo Kids' recent uploads cover healthy habits and safety (brushing teeth, bath time, handwashing, bus safety rules) alongside colours, fruits and phonics, showing routine songs are a core, steady earner for top nursery channels.

Hey Bear Sensory has about 3.4B views from only 95 videos (about 35M per video) with dancing fruit and veggie characters on plain black backgrounds and wordless funk, house and disco tracks; its biggest hits are 10 to 27 minute mixes (Smoothie Mix 383M, Fruit Salad Dance Party 334M), while its recent 1 to 5 minute uploads average only about 5M.

CreatorDB's study of 417 surging channels over 500K subscribers (Sep 2026) found 24% post 60+ times a month and 42% at least daily, but median subscribers gained per upload were about 98,800 for channels posting under 8 times a month, 16,100 for regular, 6,100 for heavy and only 1,900 for the heaviest posters: volume buys reach, not loyalty.

CoComelon's Netflix viewing fell 30% in H2 2025 and the brand moves to Disney+ in January 2027, while creator led YouTube shows (Ms Rachel, CrunchLabs) rose, so the market now rewards a warm personality and fresh feel over a polished nursery rhyme factory.

Little Baby Bum (41.6M subscribers, 44.8B views) has had flat or falling subscribers since early 2025 yet still earns about 110 to 140M views a month, proof that an old nursery catalogue lives on recommendations and repeat viewing, not new subscribers.

All five of Little Baby Bum's most viewed videos are Wheels on the Bus variants: Halloween Wheels on the Bus (275M), Ten Little Buses (112M and 69M), Bus Wash (60M) and Wheels on the Bus Underwater (56M), so a single proven song re set in new places and seasons is a repeatable hit engine.

Little Baby Bum's newest Shorts are counting songs with a twist on a known rhyme ('Ten Shiny Stars Roll Out of Bed', 5 Nov 2026), reaching about 53K views in under two days, so classic counting down structures (ten in the bed, five little ducks) adapt well to Shorts.

In Tubefilter's most viewed list for the week of 8 Nov 2026, kid duo and family channels fill the top: Cadel and Mia 890M weekly views (down from first to third), Sierra and Rhia English and Sierra and Rhia FAM both up 7%, Keizo and Friends climbing from 29th to 20th, so sibling and friend pairs are the format kids binge most.

GoBooBoo (4.29M subscribers) gets about 36M views a month from only 197 videos, roughly 180K monthly views per video, and its all time hit Baby Finger Where Are You passed 930M views, so a small catalogue of well made songs can outearn a huge one.

Junior Squad has 1,164 videos and 5.45M subscribers but only about 4.4M views in the last 28 days, and its newest 2 minute rhyme got about 3K views in two days, a warning that high volume rhyme uploads without strong recurring characters stall.

GoBooBoo titles pair an original named song with a known rhyme hook (Boo Boo Song plus Wheels on the Ambulance, 150M) and its second biggest hit is a gentle fear song, Something in the Dark (194M), so mild spooky or brave in the dark themes work for preschoolers.

Stomp! Stomp! Rhinos!, a kids feelings channel that teaches calming down and mindfulness through rhythm, stomping and play, reached 12M+ views in 195 countries, 101K watch hours and 9,800 subscribers within 12 months from 300+ videos and Shorts, so big views can come with few subscribers on kids channels.

The Kiboomers (Canada, 4.04M subscribers) earns a steady 50 to 55M views a month while posting only one new video each Friday, and vidIQ models about 37K USD a month, far more per view than mass upload rhyme channels, because its catalogue is evergreen circle time music teachers replay.

All five of The Kiboomers' most viewed videos are movement games: Going on a Dragon Hunt (37.4M), Freeze Dance Song 2 (31.1M), Red Light Freeze Dance (30M), Going on a Dinosaur Hunt (23.4M) and Floor is Lava 2 Freeze Dance (18.2M), and sequels of a winning game (Freeze Dance 2, Floor is Lava 2) do as well as originals.

The Kiboomers' newest upload is a seasonal movement game, Shake Your Santa Hat (6 Nov 2026), so classroom channels release Christmas dance songs in the first week of November to catch teachers' December planning.

Kaboochi (2.17M subscribers, 2,225 videos) gets about 11.6M views a month, and its biggest hits are theme twists on the Finger Family song (Football Finger Family 29M, Planet Finger Family 17M), so a known song frame plus a new theme is its main growth trick, though sheer volume gives low views per video.

In Tubefilter's most subscribed list for the week of 8 Nov 2026 only three kids or family channels made the top 50: Pokemon Kids TV (Japan, about 400K new subscribers, down 20%), Cadel and Mia (about 300K) and VocaVoca Kids Songs (US, about 300K), so a nursery song channel like VocaVoca can still out gain most of YouTube.

CoComelon's owner Moonbug launched The Melon Patch on YouTube (season 2 from 23 Jul 2026), a live action show led by a music teacher host with acoustic nursery rhymes, original songs and real children singing along in new 15 minute episodes every other week, a move towards the warm human host style Ms Rachel proved.

Moonbug's content chief says the company is YouTube first, a brand must build a strong YouTube audience before toys, live tours and streaming deals, and content should fit each viewing moment from a short clip on a phone in the car to living room co viewing; its 2026 slate adds a Little Angel spin off with pop songs and pretend play for ages 3 to 5.

VocaVoca's last 28 days to 12 Nov 2026 brought about 1.42B views versus 2.91B in October, so even a fast rising song channel roughly halved its monthly reach once the Halloween spike passed; seasonal surges must be followed at once by the next season's songs.

VocaVoca's newest upload, a good manners song ('May I Please?', 11 Nov 2026), reached about 133K views in its first 13 hours, more evidence that manners, habits and safety songs are this channel's engine after Halloween.

Jasmin and James (Germany based duo, 43.1M subs, 79.9B views from about 26,700 videos) get their best recent Shorts from behind the scenes bloopers (120K to 188K views) and 'Can you do it?' challenges, ahead of plain trend tutorials; a Bro Bros bloopers Short (a brother slipping on a dance move) and a direct 'Can you do it?' challenge are cheap, proven formats.

Jasmin and James lean on movie character trend tutorials (Spider-Verse costume trends); we skip anything using protected characters and copy only the tutorial format (slow step, then full speed) with our own Bros.

Acamar Films (Bing) launched Again! Again!, a gentle paced public service style preschool channel on YouTube in June 2026 with presenter led themed blocks, live streamed segments and nine starter titles; Acamar already runs 67 channels in 33 languages with 1.3M viewing hours a day.

Lalafun's top recent breakout 'Catch the Black Sheep! Baa Baa Song' reached 33M views in about two months, 30 times its median, and its other hits follow the same title shape: an urgent mission for the baby ('Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider', 'Paramedic Cures the Boo Boos'), then a well known rhyme anchor, one or two emojis and the channel tag.

Lalafun has only 77 videos but 158M views, uploads about three long videos a week averaging nearly 18 minutes with no Shorts, and its estimated audience is the US 44%, UK 17%, Brazil 17%, Turkey 11% and Poland 11%.

Super Simple Songs' best recent upload is a remake of its own 'The Animals On The Farm' (38M views, 5.7 times median), and it now publishes 'High Contrast Kids Video' versions of songs (Fruit Is Yummy, 11M), so remaking our own proven hits and making high contrast baby editions are both proven moves.

Super Simple Songs still uploads only about once a week, recent uploads average about 30 minutes, long form gives 96% of its views, and its estimated audience is the US 53%, UK 18%, Canada 12%, Japan 12% and Vietnam 6%, showing English songs travel to ESL markets in Asia.

Kids Diana Show's recent breakouts are scale challenges ('10 vs 100 vs 1,000,000 House Decorating', 43M) and opposite pairs ('Ice Princess vs Fire Princess', 57M) plus story compilations, formats an animated channel can copy as '1 snowman vs 100 snowmen vs 1,000,000 snowmen' style songs.

Big kids channels keep about 85 to 90% evergreen content and only 10 to 15% trend based (Lalafun and Kids Diana 90/10, Super Simple Songs 85/15), a useful split for planning our 14 songs a week: roughly 12 evergreen and 2 trend songs.

Cocomelon's Instagram (about 790K followers, 1.1K posts) runs as a parenting humour and toddler life account aimed at adults, averaging about 214K Reel plays but only 0.26% likes per follower and about 10 posts in two weeks, far smaller than its YouTube reach.

Rhymington Square (Canada, 311K subscribers) has 291M views from only 74 videos, about 3.9M per video, built on original friendly monster songs about toddler life; few, strong, rewatchable songs can out earn a big volume of weaker ones.

Rhymington Square's recent breakouts are everyday toddler moments told as songs ('It's Way Too Hot Today' 17M, 'Let's Blow A Bubble' 16M, 'My Glasses' 10M) and numbered sequels of proven hits ('There's A Monster In My Tummy #2', 'Open Shut Them #2').

Seasonal holiday songs are Rhymington Square's largest topic cluster (15 of 74 videos) and about 24% of its content is trend based, with audience in the US 61%, Canada 21%, UK 12% and Australia 6%, so holiday songs suit North American audiences especially.

TinkaBop Baby Sensory, a young baby sensory music channel, had 11 videos and about 5K subscribers by Sep 2026 with a gentle bath time song as its best (18K views), showing how slowly a new routine song channel grows and how bath, wake up and bedtime routines lead in the baby niche.

OutlierKit flags dependence on YouTube Kids distribution and on one signature voice as key risks for small baby music channels, so Bro Bros should keep the Bros' voices consistent but build reach on main YouTube, Shorts and Instagram too.

Cocomelon's biggest 2026 breakouts stack two proven hooks in one title ('Yes Yes Finger Family Playground Song' 52M views, 14 times its median; 'The Rainbow Popsicle Cafe + Super Muffin Man' 21M) or revive a novelty classic ('Bananaphone' 40M).

Cocomelon still uploads about three videos a week averaging about 5.5 minutes with almost no Shorts, keeps about 95% evergreen content, and roughly 10% of recent uploads are Hello Kitty and Sanrio collaborations, showing big brands now team up with other kids IP for fresh reach.
Cocomelon's estimated audience is the US 50%, India 17%, UK 17%, Canada 11% and Australia 6%, so India is now as big as the UK for English nursery songs.

Ms Rachel uploads only about 1.4 videos a month but each runs about 45 minutes, and her top titles lead with a parent search promise ('Baby Learning with Ms Rachel', 'Learn to Talk', 'First Words', '2 Year Old Milestones') before 'Nursery Rhymes & Kids Songs', proof that parents search by developmental goal.

An exploratory academic study of English and Portuguese AI made kids videos (2022 to 2024) found music and stories are the main content types, most such videos get low view counts with a few viral exceptions, and many sit on a spectrum of partial AI use; a Bro Bros edge is visible human craft (story, choreography, edits) on top of AI tools.
leaves.src: AoIR Selected Papers (Mintz and Bozzi), Jan 2026

leaves.t: Super Simple Songs turned 20 in 2026 with over 70M subscribers and 90B views; it began in 2006 as teachers abroad posting songs to help children learn English, so English learning classrooms worldwide are a lasting audience Bro Bros can serve with clear, slow, repeatable English lyrics.

Super Simple's maker Skyship moved to a self funded Toronto studio in 2015 with 40+ in house animators, musicians, puppeteers and educators, and works with researchers (an Oxford University Press project in Spain) on how music shapes early learning, using that teaching credibility to win parents and teachers.

Moonbug says Little Angel has over 150M YouTube subscribers and about 1.4B monthly views across 25 languages, and it programmes its linear channels in 100+ countries around daily routines from morning to bedtime (meals, tooth brushing, bedtime), the same routine slots Bro Bros playlists should be named for.

Moonbug's 2026 plan is YouTube first but non exclusive ('be on every platform where kids and families are'), extending hit IP into Spotify music, toys and live tours, and it is pushing hardest into Southern Europe (Spain and France), a sign those markets reward kids brands now.

Mother Goose Club licensed its YouTube library to the SKIDOS ad free learning app for ages 2 and up (Aug 2026), showing a later revenue path for a big kids song catalogue: subscription learning apps that pay for familiar, education framed content.

Moonbug's Blippi spinoff Meekah opened on its own YouTube channel on 7 Nov 2026, warmed up by a single music video ('Happy Place') on 2 Nov, with roughly 15 minute episodes for ages 3 to 6 every other Saturday.

Meekah episodes alternate short bursts of dance and physical play with short pauses, a move then rest rhythm built on UCLA backed learning principles that Bro Bros can copy inside long compilations (dance, calm breath, dance).

Moonbug launched Big Feelings Music in Sept 2026, offering label services, publishing administration and YouTube distribution to outside children's music creators, a possible future partner route for an independent kids song brand.

Pinkfong is releasing the soundtrack of its 5 Dec Baby Shark Christmas sing along film in two waves (10 Nov and 27 Nov), 15 tracks with seven new songs, and uses an on screen MC character to lead audience participation, a staged drop pattern we can copy for a December song pack.

ChuChu TV grew by refreshing old nursery rhymes with new stories instead of making lullabies, and even early on earned 40 to 50% of revenue abroad (mostly UK, US and Canada) while Vietnam gave many views but little revenue.

Kids Diana's network is 32 channels in 17 languages with about 429M subscribers and 261B views; its 27 smaller language channels together have about 240M subscribers, more than the 138M main channel, showing that separate dubbed channels can outgrow the original.

Kids Diana's largest language channels are Spanish (41.1M), Arabic (30.9M), English (30M) and Hindi (29.4M), and about 12 of its channels run 24/7 live streams, while the main channel has added multi language audio tracks.

In Tubefilter's week of 8 Nov 2026, Spanish preschool channel El Tren Nam Nam dropped 52% (from No. 7 to No. 39) while Keizo and Friends climbed from No. 29 to No. 20 and two Sierra and Rhia channels sat in the top 8, showing how fast kids channel weekly views swing.

A Spanish kids channel admitted to the YouTube Kids app about a month after an official partner submitted it saw views grow 396%, with the app supplying 67.4% of its traffic, so getting Bro Bros reviewed for the Kids app is one of the biggest single growth levers once the catalogue is clean.

AIR's order of fixes for a stalled kids channel is trust signals first (clean thumbnails, remove weak old videos, resolve yellow icons), then dubbed audio tracks, then 24/7 streams, because languages and streams only work once YouTube trusts the channel.

BabyBus (44.2M subscribers, about 186M views in the last 28 days) has slowed sharply in 2026: about 100K new subscribers a month versus 300K to 700K in 2024, and monthly views fell from about 328M in April to 218M in October 2026.

BabyBus's most watched videos are still older evergreen songs (Rainbow Juice colours song from 2022 at 147M views), while its 2025 and 2026 'Sharing is Caring' good habit songs are the clear outliers at 10 to 16 times the channel's normal views, so manners and feelings songs keep pulling new viewers.

CoComelon's Portuguese channel posted 48 uploads between 31 Aug and 9 Nov 2026 (29 long videos, median 5:22, and 19 Shorts, median 22 seconds), roughly five uploads a week split about 3 long to 2 Shorts.

CoComelon's dubbed channels tag brand new songs with a star and the word NEW at the start of the title and still publish 30 minute holiday compilations, and their best recent long uploads are simple action or routine songs (a rain go away song at 4.7M, a car wash song at 2.4M).

Brazil's kid pop acts show how fast a school age music brand can grow: duo Kysha e Mine reached about 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in roughly a year with a school themed series, and MC Divertida has about 18.3M subscribers; their label has psychologists review lyrics and scripts, which it says wins parent and school trust.

Disney Jr. tests stories with children through an internal panel and feeds results to writers (its programming head calls young viewers 'our bosses'), and grew SuperKitties over three years with 60 minute specials, shorts and long episodes side by side, so one Bro Bros song should also ship as a Short, a long video and a compilation slot.

Pinkfong launched 'Baby Shark Boy' in Aug 2026 with the single 'WAVE', which opens on the familiar Baby Shark melody and grows into upbeat electropop with trap beats and a featured K-pop rapper, plus a point choreography that nods to the original dance but stays easy to follow, a way to keep kids who have outgrown nursery songs.

Pinkfong's new Baby Shark musical (2 Dec 2026 to 28 Mar 2027, Seoul) has no seats: children roam seven themed zones, join missions, hold colour changing microphones and their voices become part of the music, and the story is about recovering a lost rhythm and melody, showing that 'help us fix the song' participation is the brand's next step.

Russian language family creator Sasha Show grew from about 1.2 to 2.2M new subscribers a month in mid 2026 to 9.47M in October (18.3M total, 633M views in the last 28 days) with only about 46 uploads a year of toy, candy and bath challenge videos and remixes, yet vidIQ models only about 17K USD of earnings, showing how little very large Shorts led kids audiences can pay.

Toys and Colors' franchise reported 136M subscribers and 149B lifetime views, with its top three YouTube channels reaching 348M unique viewers and 11.6B minutes of watch time in 90 days, and its holiday special came with an original single released on Spotify, Amazon Music and Apple Music, so a kids channel's holiday song should also live on music apps.

Sasha Show's titles lean on famous toy and candy brands and extreme 'who will win' challenges, a growth route Bro Bros should not copy (brand names invite claims and do not suit made for kids quality rules), but its question style titles ('Who will...?') match the mystery question hooks already in our playbook.

Bebefinn's main English channel (37.3M subscribers, 25.1B views, 1,086 videos since Mar 2022) still adds about 370M views a month, but its subscriber gains fell to 100K to 300K a month in 2026 from 500K to 1.3M a month in 2024 and 2025, the same plateau BabyBus and Little Angel show, so the biggest 3D song brands are no longer growing fast and newer channels have room.

Bebefinn's newest upload, 'We Are Car Mechanics! Let's Fix the Car!' (13 Nov 2026), drew about 133K views in 13 hours with a title built as emoji, pretend play job and action call, and its all time top video is a 2022 good morning wake up routine song (775M views), so pretend play jobs and daily routine songs remain the brand's core.

vidIQ models Bebefinn's main channel at only about 97K USD a month of ad revenue from roughly 370M monthly views (about 0.26 USD per 1,000 views), confirming that made for kids song views earn little per view and that brands like Pinkfong earn mainly from streaming deals, toys and live shows.

Indonesian kids family channel Keizo and Friends (started Dec 2022) reached about 9.9M subscribers and 39.2B views from 1,998 uploads by Oct 2026, adding about 1.65B views and 390K subscribers in 28 days, with a new upload passing 1.5M views in 14 hours; vidIQ models only about 9K USD a month, so its scale comes from Shorts views in a low pay market.

AIR's study of 282 kids channels found the largest (10M to 50M monthly views) earned the most total revenue at 16+ videos a month, but each video then earned only about 165 USD against about 2,161 USD per video for channels posting one or two a month, so our 14 songs a week buy reach, while a few polished flagship songs per month carry most of the money.

Keizo and Friends' all time top video is from 7 Dec 2025 (about 626M views), a December upload that kept growing for a year, another sign that early December family videos get a long tail and our holiday songs should be live by the first week of December.

Skyship's live action 'Super Simple Play with Caitie!' (Canada, 5.25M subscribers) steadied at about 47 to 58M views a month through 2026 after a 2025 peak (332M in Apr 2025); its all time hits are 'Here Comes the Fire Truck' (109M), the colour hunt 'I See Something Blue' (78M), a Halloween knock knock song (63M) and the freeze game 'Can You Dance and Stop?' (50M), and vidIQ models about 46K USD a month.

US rhyme channel Super Supremes (4M subscribers, 960 videos) has been flat since late 2025 at about 3 to 7M views a month and its newest Short (9 Nov 2026, a fire truck wheels song) drew only about 1.8K views in five days, showing that a big but stale subscriber base no longer guarantees views for generic rhyme remakes.

Across both channels the top songs are fire trucks, Halloween and colour or freeze games, and Caitie's newest upload (12 Nov) is already a Christmas party song, so Super Simple starts holiday uploads in mid November.

Five of the ten most viewed YouTube videos of all time are children's songs (led by Baby Shark Dance and CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus), together estimated at about 84M USD in ad revenue, proof that one evergreen kids song can earn for years.

Lalafun's 'Learning Time!' side channel (605K subscribers, only 91 videos) was flat until May 2026, then jumped to about 34 to 61M views a month from July to October; its hits put a verb and a baby helper into a classic rhyme title ('Catch the Black Sheep!' 76M, 'Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider!' 31M, 'Animals Go to a Picnic! Wheels on the Bus' 20M).

Funny Lala, Lalafun's kindergarten channel (1.77M subscribers, 326 videos since Jun 2023), still gains about 80K subscribers and 72M views a month, and all of its top five videos are remixes of rhymes into little stories (a rainy farm 'where is the sun?' remix leads at 31.5M).

Lalafun's Canada feed has 2,408 videos and 1.64M subscribers, yet its 31 Oct 2026 toothbrush song drew only 495 views in 41 hours while the brand's young Learning Time channel got about 25K views in under two days on its newest upload, so the algorithm rewards fresh focused channels over huge back catalogues.

Both healthy Lalafun channels title new songs as an action plus a familiar character or animal ('Catch the Little Frogs with Baby Lala!', 'Five Little Ducklings and Mommy Duck'), mixing a known rhyme cue with a small adventure, which is a title pattern we can copy with our own originals ('Catch the Snowflakes with Little Bro!').

Jason Vlogs, two brothers' kids channel that grew from 23M to 46M+ subscribers with a peak of about 1B views in one month, keeps a baseline of one main video a week with extras as bonuses, plans and batches weeks ahead, and runs on a core team of five.

Jason Vlogs brainstorms about 30 ideas a week and produces only 3, filtering by current platform trends, what kids already react to and whether the idea stays fun and teaches something, a stricter filter than making every idea that comes up.

ChuChu TV's newest English uploads (Oct to Nov 2026) are 24 to 34 minute story and learning compilations: 'Celebrate and Shine', a combined Diwali and Christmas story video, reached about 197K views in 16 days, a surprise egg colour song about 140K in 9 days and a learning story set about 15K in 2 days, so even a 98M subscriber channel's new uploads start small and the library carries it.

ChuChu TV tested a 2 minute read along toddler story with copy the duck play actions ('Hello, Ducklings!'), which drew about 94K views in 25 days, close to its long compilations, showing short copy me action stories are a cheap format worth testing beside songs.

Little Angel Playtime (3.24M subscribers) fell from about 10.5M monthly views in Aug 2026 to 8.6M, 7.5M and then 4.9M in October, and its newest song ('Eye Tests Are Not Scary!', 14 Nov) had under 1K views after 11 hours, showing that even a famous brand's spin off channel fades when it keeps posting small routine topics without fresh hooks.

Little Angel and Friends (7.3M subscribers, about 26M views in Oct 2026) earns mostly from 2021 to 2022 songs: Baa Baa Black Sheep 601M, a bedtime 'Monsters Under the Bed' song 210M and a lollipops, balloons and sunglasses colours song 205M; its new Baby John Wheels on the Bus vehicle song had about 3.7K views in 10 hours.

Super Simple Songs' uploads from late August to mid October 2026 were mostly 'Top 20' themed mixes (about 0.8 to 1.2M views each) and two 'Super Simple Live!' Halloween streams, while a single party song, 'Everybody Celebrate' (27 Aug), reached 6M, the clear outlier; a celebration song for any party day can outperform themed compilations.

Pinkfong launched Kikipuppup (with Japan's TBS) on YouTube first, in English, Japanese and Korean, as about 3 minute slapstick episodes with a cat, a dog and a grumpy rival, and is rolling out a wordless comedy (SEALOOK) in Russia, so the biggest song brand is adding short, dialogue light comedy that travels without dubbing.

Pinkfong keeps refreshing Baby Shark through partner remixes: a 'Do The Shark' remix in Doggyland's style, a Baby Shark and Peppa Pig mash up for the song's 10th anniversary (26 Dec 2025), and a Bebefinn medley with the London Symphony Orchestra; a hit song can be re released many times in new styles.

The Blocks Universe (Numberblocks, Alphablocks) launched its first Christmas single, 'Making Christmas Magical' with K-pop group FIFTY FIFTY, as two videos of the same song a week apart (a live action dance video on 28 Nov, the animated video on 5 Dec) plus a printables hub, a model for getting two premieres out of one holiday song.

Blippi's strongest Shorts of early November 2026 are timed challenges and playground games: 'Can Blippi build a rocket in 45 seconds?' (about 130K views, 2x its usual) and 'Red Light Green Light with kids' (about 198K), so a 'Can the Bro Bros build a snowman in 30 seconds?' countdown Short fits what kids are clicking now.

Blippi's titles in November follow one pattern: a direct question with the character's name plus a challenge or a 'what if' ('What would Blippi look like as an animal?', 'Can a fire truck be as fast as a race car?'), with one or two emojis; the same pattern works for us as 'Can Vihaan ...?' or 'What if the Bro Bros ...?' Shorts titles.

Blippi still alternates 15 minute episodes with 1.5 to 2 hour compilations, and the 2 hour vehicle race (12 Nov) is its top outlier at about 2x, so for a strong brand very long vehicle compilations still pay even after YouTube cut the boost for ultra long videos in 2025.

Blippi's 3 November dance collab with Doggyland (ice cream truck dance party, 2:48) scored only about half its normal views, a reminder that a collab or a single dance video does not beat a strong concept like a challenge or a vehicle race.

Junior Squad Nursery Rhymes has 5.45M subscribers yet its new uploads get only about 2K to 3K views each in the first week and 4.4M views in 28 days across 1,164 videos, so a big old back catalogue does not lift new uploads; fresh concepts and packaging decide each video.

Junior Squad started Christmas on 5 and 6 Nov 2026 (a Santa finger family Short, its best recent Short at about 9.4K views, and a Christmas version of its ambulance song), while its October outlier was a 75 second Frankenstein dance party song at about 19K views, so short themed dance songs and an early Christmas switch are the safe seasonal plays.

CoComelon Brasil's new Portuguese 'Rain Rain Go Away' ('Vá Embora, Chuva', 3:01, 17 Oct 2026) reached about 4.7M views in under a month, about 36 times the channel's usual, and a two song combo ('Lá na lagoa & Os Patinhos', 5:55) reached 1.7M, so re sung classic rhymes are the breakout engine for a Portuguese track.

CoComelon Brasil had no Christmas video among its last 48 uploads by 10 Nov 2026, while English kids channels switched in the first week of November, so Brazilian Christmas songs can go live later (late November to mid December, when the summer school holidays start).

CoComelon Brasil's Shorts are only 11 to 27 seconds (find the hidden JJ, making a JJ snowman or doll, a magic fruit salad) and draw 3K to 92K views, against 12K to 4.7M for its long songs, so even for the biggest brand the local language Shorts are a side feed and long songs do the heavy lifting.

CoComelon Brasil marks every new long song with a '⭐NOVO⭐' (new) prefix and ends each title with the same brand and category tag, a cheap packaging habit that tells returning parents which upload is fresh; a 'NEW' star prefix on our newest song of the day is worth testing.

ChuChu TV's main channel (98.2M subscribers, 61B views) gained no net subscribers in the 28 days to mid November 2026 and its most watched video is a 30 minute classics compilation led by 'Rain Rain Go Away' (109M views), showing that a giant catalogue can stall while old compilations keep earning.

Rain songs keep winning across brands in late 2026 (CoComelon Brasil's 36x rain song, ChuChu TV's top compilation, our own rain themed Didi story among our better Reels), so an original Bro Bros rain song with puddle jumps and umbrella moves is a safe evergreen bet.

Bebefinn's Portuguese channel (about 9.1M subscribers) gained about 150K subscribers and 296M views in the 28 days to 24 Oct 2026, roughly twice CoComelon Brasil's size and still growing fast, so a newer brand can overtake the incumbent in a dubbed language within about three years.

Bebefinn's Japanese channel (1.62M subscribers) pulled about 108M views in 28 days and adds 50K to 60K subscribers a month, the same monthly views as BabyBus Japan with a quarter of the subscribers, so in Japan a fresh brand's new videos still get recommended while old catalogues plateau.

Bebefinn Japanese grew most in January (+110K) and June 2026 (+90K) and least in April and May (+30K), matching school holidays and rainy season in Japan, so Japanese audio tracks should launch before the winter break and the June rainy season.

Bebefinn's newest local uploads are practical life lessons: a Portuguese 'never open the door to strangers' safety song (24 Oct 2026) and a Japanese 'what do we wear on a rainy day?' dressing song (6 Nov), both built as a question the child answers, which supports our safety and routine songs with a question hook.

Bebefinn Portuguese's biggest hit is an episode of a shark finger family song (about 60M views, over 100x the channel average), showing that a brand's signature character song re sung locally can carry an entire language channel.

Lalafun Nursery Rhymes (15.1M subscribers) is one of 2026's fastest growing preschool song channels: about 139M views in April, then 585M to 722M every month from May to October with 500K to 700K new subscribers a month.

Lalafun uploads about three videos a week, almost all long form (recent average about 18 minutes), which shows a mostly long form preschool channel can still grow fast in 2026 without leaning on Shorts.

BabyBus's English channel (44.2M subscribers) is steady rather than growing: about 186M to 257M views a month through 2026 and 100K new subscribers a month, flat in October; its newest upload (12 Nov) is a good habits 'Boo Boo Song' that drew about 46K views in 13 hours.

By 13 November 2026 neither BabyBus English nor Lalafun had posted a Christmas video (Lalafun's newest is a 'Sharing is Great!' manners song, 158K views in under two days), so big preschool brands start Christmas late and an early, original Christmas song still has room.

VocaVoca (US nursery songs) is 2026's breakout kids song channel: monthly views grew from about 368M in January to 1.11B in July, 1.82B in August, 2.29B in September and 2.91B in October, and subscribers from 4.9M to 10.5M.

VocaVoca is cooling in November 2026: about 1.46B views in the 28 days to 15 Nov, roughly half its October pace, though it still adds about 1.16M subscribers a month and 300K a week (Tubefilter, week of 8 Nov), a reminder that kids song surges can halve within weeks.

VocaVoca's newest upload, 'Toothy and Tootsie Help the Toy Train Find All Colors' (14 Nov 2026, about 121K views in 11 hours), combines three proven hooks at once: named helper characters, a mission verb in the title and this season's toy train theme, plus a colours learning tag.

VocaVoca's all time top videos are practical life skill songs from 2021 to 2022 (The Dentist Song 164M, Taking Care of Baby 68M, Police Officer Song 52M, Stranger Danger Song 42M, Buckle Up Song 37M), more proof that safety and routine songs keep earning for years.

Pokémon Kids TV has 44.8M subscribers and gains about 1.2M a month (400K in the week of 8 Nov, #23 worldwide) yet draws only about 71M views a month, so a big brand's subscriber surge does not mean views; we should judge competitors and ourselves by monthly views and returning viewers, not subscribers.

Super Simple Songs (47.3M subscribers, about 65B views) is still growing in 2026: monthly views rose from about 446M in February to 574M in September and 592M in October, with 100K to 200K new subscribers a month, proof that a mature brand keeps rising through steady themed uploads.

Super Simple Songs' newest song 'Scrubbity Rubbity Doo' (wash your hands and face, 5 Nov 2026) reached about 915K views in nine days; a silly made up word in the title plus a hygiene routine is exactly our playbook's nonsense chant and healthy habit formula.

Super Simple Songs' biggest videos add a new action or a puppet cast to a familiar song ('If You're Happy and You Know It Spin Around' 176M, 'Five Little Speckled Frogs' with frog puppets 164M, '500 Ducks' 214M, the puppet food song 'Are You Hungry?' 183M), so a known tune with one surprising action twist is a proven long term hit.

By 15 November 2026 Super Simple Songs, BabyBus English and Lalafun had all not yet posted a Christmas song, while smaller channels such as Junior Squad started in early November, so the big preschool brands seem to time Christmas releases for late November or December.

Danny Go! (5.43M subscribers) gets about 160M to 210M views every month of 2026 from just 131 videos, adding 100K to 160K subscribers a month; a few big, carefully made movement videos can out earn hundreds of quick uploads.

Danny Go!'s newest video, the 'Burning ENERGY! Don't Stop Moving Challenge' (9 Sep 2026), reached about 21.5M views in two months; naming a dance song a 'challenge' with a clear goal (never stop moving) suits older preschoolers and school classroom brain breaks.

All five of Danny Go!'s top videos are pretend danger movement games with sequels: 'Quicksand, Lava, Sharks' compilation 270M, 'The Floor Is Lava 2: Into the Volcano!' 263M, 'The Floor is Lava Dance!' 223M, a spooky spiders version 208M and 'Sharks in the Water 2: Rise of the Shark King!' 202M, so a winning game should get numbered part 2 and seasonal versions.

Bounce Patrol (Australia, 34M subscribers, 28.7B views) has stalled: about 89M views in the 28 days to 27 Oct 2026 with no subscriber change, and its Halloween upload drew only about 371K views in 24 days while its top hits ('Fruit So Yummy' 335M, Wheels on the Bus remixes) are years old, a warning that live action remix channels without new characters lose momentum.

CoComelon's main channel (203M subscribers, about 230B views) gets about 1.2B to 1.6B views a month in 2026 after 2.18B in January, with roughly 1M new subscribers every other month; even the biggest kids channel is flat to slightly down, so its audience share is slowly opening to newer brands.

CoComelon's newest upload (14 Nov 2026) is 'Snowy Holiday Ski Race! JJ VS CODY', a friendly winter race between two characters rather than a Christmas song, about 203K views in its first day or so; a gentle 'Big Bro VS Little Bro' snow race with a tie and a hug at the end fits the same winter competition hook.

CoComelon's all time top videos reset classic rhymes in everyday places or routines: 'Humpty Dumpty Grocery Store' 1.57B, 'Yes Yes Fruits Song' 1.24B, 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star' 878M, 'Pasta Song' 417M and 'Fire Truck Wash Song' 402M, supporting our rule of familiar tune plus everyday setting.

LooLoo Kids, a 3D animated nursery rhyme brand, has about 62.8M subscribers and 43.2B views from only about 985 videos and still uploads (latest 13 Nov 2026), proof that a small catalogue of long compilations can build a giant channel.

vidIQ's older snapshot of LooLoo Kids showed about 2 uploads a week with an average length of about 31 minutes and a low engagement rate (0.21%), the classic pattern of long, passively watched compilations.

LooLoo runs separate channels per language (Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, French, Arabic and more); the Spanish one alone has 15.1M subscribers and about 154M views in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026, so dedicated dub channels can grow into big channels of their own.

LooLoo's Spanish channel gained 200K to 600K subscribers a month in early 2025 but mostly 0 to 100K a month in 2026, while views stayed around 100M to 150M a month, a sign that old rhyme channels keep views but are losing new fans.

LooLoo's newest Spanish upload (13 Nov 2026) stacks three classic songs plus a learning tag in one title ('Los Pollitos + Rompe la Piñata + La Vaca Lechera, Animales de la Granja'), the same multi hook title stacking Cocomelon uses.

Bounce Patrol has about 34M subscribers but CreatorDB shows zero subscriber growth over the 365 days to Oct 2026 and only about one upload every few weeks, another big kids song channel living on its back catalogue.

Bounce Patrol's biggest 2026 uploads are collaborations with a famous puppet show ('Where is Elmo? (Hidey Tag)' 11.2M views, 'Ball Pit Party' 8M) while its own new songs (Rainbow Disco colours song, 30 Oct 2026) sit near 270K, so borrowed fame lifts old channels far more than fresh songs do.

Bounce Patrol's top video overall is a seek and find song ('Can You Find the Yummy Fruit?', 18.2M) and its hide and seek collab is its 2026 leader, which adds to the evidence that 'can you find it?' games are one of the strongest kids song formats.

A July 2026 ranking of kids exercise and movement channels lists Bounce Patrol (34M), Jack Hartmann (5.5M), Danny Go! (5.0M), GVO Kids (4.2M), Cosmic Kids Yoga (2.0M) and GoNoodle (1.7M) as the leaders, the field our dance songs compete in on classroom screens.

Bounce Patrol's Halloween compilation built on a marching song ('Halloween Ants Go Marching & More', 3 Oct 2026, 517K) outperformed its newer original upload, a reminder that seasonal versions of marching and counting songs are dependable.

Toys and Colors' 2025 holiday plan was a 22 minute 'Elf Academy' special (premiered 21 Nov on its own kids streaming app, then Hulu on 27 Nov) plus a new holiday single and guest appearances by other creators, so a single longer holiday special is how big YouTube kids brands mark Christmas.

That holiday single was released on a multi creator 'Holiday Hits Snow Day Soundtrack' distributed to Spotify, Amazon Music and Apple Music, so kids brands now push their Christmas songs to audio streaming as well as YouTube; a small Bro Bros Christmas EP fits the same pattern.

Hey Bear Sensory has about 3.99M subscribers and 3.36B views from only 95 videos (about 35M views per video) and still gets about 50M views a month in 2026 while uploading less than once a month, the most efficient catalogue of any kids channel we have checked.

Hey Bear's top videos are all dancing fruit and vegetable parties with upbeat funky, disco or cumbia music (Smoothie Mix 383M, Fruit Salad Dance Party counting 1 to 10 334M, Funky Veggies Extended 279M, Disco Fruit Party 243M), so cheerful dancing food characters are a proven baby sensory hit.

Hey Bear's recent uploads average about 29 minutes and its holiday videos also travel (a Halloween fruit dress up party 98M, a Christmas themed animation 89M), so one long seasonal sensory dance video can earn for years.

Hey Bear's 'EXTENDED' and '10 mins' versions of its hits sit in its top 10 beside the originals, so extending a winning dance loop into a longer edition is a cheap way to add a strong long form video.

Disney turned Gracie's Corner's YouTube songs into a Disney+ and Disney Jr. series of 120+ short sing along videos and 18 themed compilations (first drop of 68 shorts and 7 compilations on 15 Jun 2026, with global linear and streaming rights), so a clean library of short songs plus themed compilations is exactly what TV buyers want.

Gracie's Corner reached its size with only about 307 YouTube videos (Screenwise listing), so a focused catalogue of strong original songs, not sheer volume, is what built one of the biggest new kids music brands.
Gracie's Corner launched its first live US tour with Live Nation (announced Jun 2025), showing the usual order for a YouTube song brand: grow the audience, then streaming deals and live shows.

Dave and Ava (15.9M subscribers, 12.8B views, 1,431 videos) gained zero subscribers every month from June to October 2026 while still drawing about 44M to 57M views a month, so an old 3D nursery rhyme catalogue keeps earning views long after its growth stops.

Three of Dave and Ava's five most viewed videos are Halloween songs from October 2021 (top one about 11.8M), a sign that seasonal holiday songs keep coming back every year and become a channel's evergreen best sellers.

Dave and Ava's newest upload (6 Nov 2026) is a plain 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with about 30K views in its first 2.5 days, while vidIQ models the channel at only about 28K USD a month, so classic rhymes with no fresh twist no longer move even a 16M subscriber channel.

CocoBus Nursery Rhymes has 3,113 videos but only about 10.6K subscribers and about 190K to 250K views a month in late 2026, and its newest upload (a Finger Family plus Itsy Bitsy mashup, 9 Nov) got about 1K views in 13 hours, a clear case that piling up classic rhyme mashups without characters or a hook goes nowhere.

Mother Goose Club (9.89M subscribers, 12B views, 1,742 videos) gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 31 Oct 2026 and only about 10K in its best 2026 month, while views drifted between about 19M and 25M a month, and vidIQ models it at about 27K USD a month: another veteran rhyme brand coasting on its catalogue.

Mother Goose Club's newest upload, a 'BOO-tiful Songs' Halloween compilation posted 29 Oct 2026, had only about 9.9K views two days later, and its recent top videos are 'song plus more' compilations (ABC, Baby Shark, phonics) of 1.6M to 4.4M views, so a seasonal compilation from an old brand no longer gets a launch push and fresh characters are what the feed rewards.

IvyBears, an animated kids franchise made with human led storytelling and AI supported production, launched on YouTube in May 2026 and by July reported 2.5M subscribers and 40M views, with its third music driven episode at 3M views in three days (company press release, unverified); a very high subscriber to view ratio like that usually signals paid promotion, so it is not a normal organic benchmark.

IvyBears calls its model a 'reversed flywheel': it sold its bear products in more than 60 countries first and only then launched animation, releasing one full episode a month toward a seven episode season plus a planned preschool science and music spin off, showing that even AI assisted brands plan seasons and spin offs, not endless one off clips.

DRAGGLiNS, an AI animated series for 4 to 8 year olds made by one solo creator without a studio, launched on YouTube in April 2026 with four episodes, a new one every Saturday, a merch store and a US trademark filing for its name, a reminder that a solo AI assisted brand like Bro Bros should secure its name and characters early.

Paramount announced (Feb 2026) a CG animated preschool series about the Ninja Turtles as young children, 30 episodes of about 4 minutes each, launching on YouTube later in 2026, so major studios now debut preschool brands on YouTube first with episodes the length of a kids song, which means more polished competition in our length band.

Boom Buddies, a US 3D nursery rhyme channel with five buddy characters who sing and dance, has 6.18M subscribers, 3.1B views and 1,150 videos but gained zero subscribers between 19 Oct and 15 Nov 2026 and earns only about 10.7M views a month (under 10K per video), showing that a big library of generic 3D rhymes stalls without fresh hooks or trend formats.

Two of Boom Buddies' five most viewed videos are Halloween songs (Monster in the Dark 19M, Halloween Finger Family 12.7M) and another is a dance instruction song (Kaboochi Dance Song 19M), next to medleys titled 'X + More Nursery Rhymes', confirming seasonal songs and follow the moves dance songs as the long lasting hits of 3D song channels.

Sheriff Labrador (BabyBus, joined Nov 2022) reached 10.9M subscribers and 7.8B views with 1,298 videos and still gained about 100K subscribers and 173M views in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026; its newest upload, an outdoor safety mystery ('The Mystery of the Popcorn'), drew 263K views in 36 hours, so a recurring detective style 'solve it and learn a safety rule' frame keeps a 3D animal brand growing.

Sheriff Labrador's most viewed videos are pretend play and alphabet games ('Cardboard World, Learn Occupations' 73M, 'ABC Surprise Box' 71M, 'Alphabet Game' 43M) plus safety stories ('Don't Play With Ants' 39M), and its titles stack the story name with plain search phrases ('Learn Occupations, Pretend Play, Preschool Cartoon'), a title pattern worth copying for Bro Bros learning songs.

Wolfoo and Friends (6.02M subscribers) gets its views from toddler care songs: a potty song 26.8M ('Yes Yes, Push the Button'), a diaper change song 15.7M and a 'mommy has a big belly' new sibling song 12.9M, while its latest Shorts get only about 2K views, more proof that parents search for songs that help with real toddler moments (potty, nappy, a new baby).

A Pakistani English and Urdu ABC channel (TinyTaleem) still shows 145K subscribers but drew only about 2K views in the 28 days to 15 Nov 2026 and lost subscribers in October, with no video above 31K views, a reminder that subscriber totals mean little for kids channels without fresh, searchable uploads.

Morphle TV (Moonbug's 3D magic pet cartoon) has 13.1M subscribers and 10.1B views from 2,263 videos but gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 23 Oct 2026 and drew only about 15M views a month (about 6.6K per video), its newest Shorts start at about 5K views, and all of its top 5 videos date from 2021 to 2023.

Morphle's biggest hits are transformation and emotion hooks in the title ('Morphing Family' 41M, 'Morphle is CRYING!' 32M, 'Giant Morphle Monster' 12M), and together with Boom Buddies' flat month it shows that huge 3D libraries stall once they stop adding fresh story hooks, while newer brands with weekly new stories (Sheriff Labrador, VocaVoca) keep growing.

Little Angel's main channel uploaded almost daily in late Sep and early Oct 2026, with most new videos at about 7K to 30K views, while its 'Brush Your Teeth Song' healthy habits video reached about 96K, so routine and habit songs still beat generic play stories even for a big brand.

Little Angel posted its Halloween dress up song on 30 Sep 2026, a full month before the day, which matches a roughly four week lead time for seasonal songs; by that rule Christmas songs should already be live by late November.

Little Angel Playtime (3.24M subs, 1,255 videos) gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 and its monthly views fell from about 15.6M in Jan 2026 to about 4.9M in Oct, with its top five videos all from 2021 and 2022, another sign that spin off channels of big brands are decaying.

Little Angel Playtime's all time hits are safety and feelings songs (No No Swimming 118M, Daddy's Little Helper 84M, Monsters in the Dark 70M, a boo boo care song 63M), and its newest upload is an 'eye tests are not scary' song, so songs that calm a child's fear of a new experience are a long lasting format.

A 'Do the Daddy and Jill Dance' Short from Little Angel (29K views) outperformed most of its long uploads that week, showing that a named family dance Short helps even a brand whose main videos are stories.

In the week of 2 to 8 Nov 2026 Cadel and Mia fell from first to third most viewed channel worldwide with weekly views down 24%, while Sierra and Rhia English rose from 8th to 6th and their FAM channel from 12th to 8th, so even giant family Shorts channels swing a quarter of their views week to week.

In CreatorDB's Sep 2026 study, Grandma Dong's 14 second rural life Shorts averaged about 71K views while the same channel's long videos had a median of only about 840, a reminder that a Shorts audience does not automatically follow to long form; Bro Bros Shorts must point clearly to the full song.

Legacy brands dominate kids demand worldwide (Sesame Street 55 years, Peppa Pig 20+, CoComelon's roots 15+) and a 10 year old action series, Miraculous, rose 98% to become the most in demand kids IP, so a new brand wins by staying consistent for years with the same characters rather than chasing one hit.

Super Simple Play with Caitie (5.25M subs, 712 videos) has held steady at about 47M to 58M views and 20K to 30K new subscribers every month of 2026, unlike most legacy kids channels that are shrinking, which suggests a warm host leading simple action songs keeps families coming back.

Caitie's biggest videos are participation songs: a fire truck song (109M), an 'I see something blue' colour spotting song (78M), a knock knock trick or treat song (63M) and 'Can You Dance and Stop?' (50M), so call and respond, spot it and freeze dance songs are the strongest formats for this audience.

Super Simple Play posted its first Christmas party Short ('It's time to party!') on 12 Nov 2026, about 12.7K views in two days, another big brand switching to Christmas content in the second week of November.

Blue Ant Media's largest ever kids slate at MIPCOM 2026 is built from short episodes: Tralala (52 x 7 minutes, a young frog and her dad, already sold to CBeebies, ABC Australia, SVT and YLE), Little Margo Stories (50 x 3 minutes) and BeddyByes (52 x 11 minutes), confirming that broadcasters now buy the same bite sized lengths that work on YouTube.

Mother Goose Club (live action costume nursery rhymes, 9.89M subscribers, 12B views) gained zero subscribers in almost every month of 2026 and only about 21M to 27M views a month, and its newest Halloween compilation (29 Oct 2026) had about 10K views, so a big legacy library of classic rhymes is now flat.

Mother Goose Club Toons, the brand's animated channel (1.08M subscribers), earns about 5M to 6M views a month in 2026 with almost no subscriber growth; its best videos are character story rhymes from 2022 to 2023 ('Lazy Mary' 8.9M, 'Five Little Ducks' 7.8M) and its 11 Nov 2026 Thanksgiving feast video got about 7.5K views in three days.

Mother Goose Club's top long videos are all 'Song + More' compilations led by one famous song (ABC Song 4.4M, Baby Shark 2.3M, The Planting Song 1.8M), which confirms that the lead song in a compilation title does the selling, so each Bro Bros compilation should be named after its single strongest song.

Cartoon Clubhouse, a CoComelon compilation channel with 12.8M subscribers and 5.7B views, gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 24 Oct 2026 and got about 26M views, while its newest upload had only 3.3K views, so even a giant brand's reupload channel now lives on its old library, not on new uploads.

Cartoon Clubhouse's top five videos are all two hour compilations from late 2022, and the two biggest are sing along karaoke versions (182M views for a Wheels on the Bus karaoke), so on screen lyric sing along cuts of a proven hit can outperform the original song video.

Pancake Manor, a two person indie Canadian kids music channel mixing original songs with classic rhymes, uploads roughly once a month; its newest songs earn 51K to 85K views in one to four months while year old songs sit at 160K to 340K, so an original song keeps gaining views for about a year before it settles.

Pancake Manor earns beyond YouTube ads through music streaming, a Patreon style fan club and a shop of dolls and shirts, which shows a small original music brand can survive on several thin income lines rather than ad views alone.

leaves.t: Kids Funny Songs (7.81M subscribers) still gained about 230K subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026, and its newest song about learning to ride a bike (13 Nov) drew 62.7K views in its first two and a half days, about 966 views an hour.

Kids Funny Songs' all time biggest videos are songs about one everyday moment a toddler meets, such as getting a shot at the doctor (270M), a copycat game (160M) and not playing on a manhole cover (120M), so a single real life moment with a small fear or a game in it beats a general theme.

Pinkfong's 3D preschool series Dinolings (a little T rex at Dino School learning numbers, colours and friendship) passed 1M YouTube subscribers and 160M views by May 2026 after its second season lifted views 639% over the first, helped by Netflix top 10 placings in the US, UK, Canada and Australia.

Zoobees, a nursery rhyme channel launched in March 2023, got all five of its biggest videos (Wheels on the Bus 23.6M, Finger Family 9.8M, Johny Johny 5M) within its first two months, but now sits at 179K subscribers and about 1M views a month, so the 2023 window when a new channel could ride classic rhyme remakes has closed.

Zoobees posted a Christmas song (five little elves playing peekaboo with Santa) on 12 Nov 2026 and it drew only about 1.9K views in its first two and a half days, showing that small rhyme channels are already in the Christmas lane by mid November but a generic seasonal rhyme alone does not break through.

A Zoobees safety remix, 'Wheels on the Ambulance', reached 4.3M views as one of its top five, a sign that putting a familiar tune on a rescue vehicle with a safety message travels better than plain rhyme covers; our own version should be an original tune about a helper vehicle, not a cover.

HeyKids' Polish song channel (856K subscribers) drew only about 3.2M views and 1K subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026, and its 14 Nov upload had 881 views after two days, roughly a fourteenth of the home grown Polish leader Spiewajace Brzdace (about 46M a month).

HeyKids Polish's biggest video by far is a song named after a cheeky little boy character (19.4M, Apr 2024), with construction machines (6.9M) and a red car (5.7M) next, so a named, mischievous kid character in the title beats generic topic songs even inside a translated network channel.

German channel Kinderlieder zum Mitsingen und Bewegen (3.47M subscribers, 4.9B views) got about 33M views and 10K subscribers in the 28 days to 15 Nov 2026; its two biggest videos are 'who took the cookie from the jar' (24.4M) and 'your bone is gone, doggy' (22.9M), both sing, dance and move songs about something going missing.

Bebefinn (37.3M subscribers) posted 'Ballet Song, EP222, I Want to Be a Ballerina!' on 14 Nov 2026 and it passed about 247K views in a day and a half; its title stacks a dance style keyword, an episode number, a child's dream line and 'Dance Song for Kids', a pattern we can copy with our own dance styles (a robot dance song, a tap dance song) for both Bros.

Super Simple Songs (47.3M subscribers) grew its monthly views steadily from about 479M in June 2026 to 592M in October, while louder channels such as Bounce Patrol and Brazil's Cleo e Cuquin stalled or fell, a sign that calm, simple, clearly sung songs are gaining in 2026.

By 15 and 16 Nov 2026 neither Bebefinn nor Super Simple Songs had a Christmas themed newest upload (their latest were a ballet song and a hand washing song), so big channels seem to hold new Christmas songs until late November, which leaves room for an early original Bro Bros Christmas song to collect search traffic first.

Omar & Hana's English channel (4.02M subscribers, 3.12B views, about 29M views a month) titled its 14 Nov 2026 upload 'Wanna Play with Me? | NO INSTRUMENTS | Islamic Series' (about 30K views in under two days), so a big faith friendly kids brand now puts 'NO INSTRUMENTS' in the title as a searchable label; a Bro Bros vocals only edit should carry the same plain label.

Omar & Hana's Malay language channel (8.67M subscribers, about 98M views in October 2026, plus 90K subscribers in 28 days) is more than three times the size of its English channel, and its top videos are 45 to 90 minute story and song compilations, so Malay is a strong language for a family friendly brand and long compilations are what Malaysian families play.

Moonbug Kids Arabic (909K subscribers, 369M views), a dubbed network channel for global shows, fell from about 2.74M monthly views in August 2026 to about 1.97M in October, and its newest dubbed upload had only about 3.7K views after three days, while a small home grown Arabic song channel like Super Dido still gets about 4M a month, so in Arabic a dub of a foreign show earns less than locally made songs with local themes.

Cocobi's Spanish channel (3.2M subscribers, 3.5B views) jumped from about 89M views in September 2026 to about 215M in October and gained 70K subscribers, and its all time top videos are 'where is...?' mysteries ('Where is the T-Rex's tail?' 21M, 'Where is my cookie?' 16.9M) plus safety songs set in one place (the amusement park 18.4M, the supermarket 18.1M).

Cocobi's newest Spanish upload (14 Nov 2026) is 'Police dog to the rescue! Catch the thief!', so a fourth big brand (after a German movement channel, an Arabic song channel and our own Reels) is betting on the missing item or chase hook; a 'Where is ...?' title with one lost object is now our safest mystery format across languages.

Miliki Family (2.59M subscribers, 1.57B views) roughly doubled its monthly views from about 19M in May 2026 to 40 to 46M in September and October, and its top videos are all 'afraid of...' coping songs: 'I Can't Sleep, Mommy! Afraid of the Dark' (381M), a boo boo safety song (43M), 'Time to Get a Shot' (36M) and a dentist song (33M), strong proof that gentle fear coping songs (dark, doctor, dentist, haircut) are among the biggest kids song topics.

Tidi Kids (2.73M subscribers, 2.5B views) also doubled from about 19M monthly views in June 2026 to about 39M in September and October with silly toilet humour and vehicles: a sing along poo poo song (56M), an opposites car song (51M), a funny car toot song (43M) and a 'Super Toot Family' song (37M), and its newest Short is a 'who tooted? maybe Brother?' mystery, so mild potty humour plus a whodunit hook is working right now.

On Bebefinn's Japanese channel (1.62M subscribers, about 125M views in October 2026) the most viewed video is the English language 'Good Morning' song with English nursery rhymes (21.4M), just ahead of its Japanese version (20.2M), and the newest upload (6 Nov) is episode 164 of a weather song series about dressing for rain, so Japanese parents also play English songs for language learning and long numbered everyday series keep paying off.

Kids Diana Show (138M subscribers) drew about 326M views in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026 with no net subscriber change, and its newest upload, a real cardboard train challenge (12 Nov), had about 152K views in a day and a half, so even the biggest family brands now live on their back catalogue.

Kids Diana Show's five most viewed videos ever (420M to 566M each) are all challenge or adventure stories: school bus rules with friends, an escape room, opening 10 doors, a maze to help a baby brother, a cube challenge; a 'what is behind the door' or 'find the way' structure is one of the strongest proven story spines for kids.

ChuChu TV's sister channel Jumblikans (5.42M subscribers, 3.3B views, 384 videos) gets only about 50K to 80K views per new upload, such as a 2 minute counting song about ten little supercars and superbikes, so a spin off channel does not inherit the main channel's reach.

LEGO and BBC Studios launched LEGO Bluey Shorts on 2 Jul 2026 as ten episodes of about 2 minutes, retelling show scenes in brick style, released weekly until 3 Sep in 12 languages at once and posted on three YouTube channels plus the show's site, a template for a short weekly mini series dubbed from day one.

Spin Master turned its Roblox game Sparkles Magical Market into a YouTube animated series and released Unicorn Academy Shorts weekly on Fridays in six languages, calling these launches the next step in its digital evolution, which shows toy brands now treat Roblox games and YouTube Shorts as starting points for kids shows.

Patty Shukla Kids TV (US, 3.98M subscribers, about 2.49B views, 901 videos) gained about 20K subscribers and 14M views in the 28 days to 15 Nov 2026, almost all from its back catalogue, since its newest upload (a 'Limbo Game Song', 9 Nov) had only about 6.9K views after five days.

Patty Shukla's most viewed video ever is a song that runs the 'hot potato' party game (about 20.4M views since 2021), more evidence that a song which IS a game families can play at a party (pass, freeze, stop on the word) keeps earning for years.

Movement song channels split into two speeds in late 2026: a few personality led ones (Danny Go!, Super Simple) still grow, while long running ones such as Patty Shukla (about 10K subscribers a month) and Bounce Patrol (flat) live on old hits, so a new channel wins by having fresh characters plus a game or dance hook, not by volume alone.

Sierra and Rhia English (15.7M subscribers, about 34.2B views, No. 6 worldwide in early Nov 2026) uploaded nine short role play videos on 3 Nov 2026 alone, each titled 'Sierra and Rhia: ' plus one kind behaviour (Sharing the Slide, Caring for Our Toys, Learning to Be Kind) and each passing about 180K to 256K tracked views within days.

That channel's strongest recent upload was a guessing game, 'Which One Is Chocolate? Role Play' (about 305K tracked views), and it had no Christmas titles by early November, showing that the top family Shorts channels run on evergreen manners and 'which one is real?' games rather than holidays, which we can match with a Bro Bros 'which one is the real cookie?' song game.

WildBrain's CG 'Strawberry Shortcake's Bake Shop' (shown at Annecy 2026) is 26 episodes of about 3 minutes for ages 4 to 8 premiering first on the brand's own YouTube channel, more proof that big studios now make 3 minute YouTube first CG episodes, the same length as a Bro Bros song.

Funlala Kids Songs (US, Lalafun branded, started Mar 2023) has about 988K subscribers, 1.31B views and 2,936 videos; it gained about 41.7M views and 20K subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 and 75.5M views in October, but that is only a third of its Sep 2025 peak (237M a month), so even big volume nursery rhyme channels have cooled over the past year.

Funlala's second most viewed video ever is a February 2026 upload, 'Choo Choo Train Song | Baby Animals Find Their Mommies' (12.9M views), showing that a simple vehicle plus baby animals plus 'find mummy' story still breaks out in 2026, while its newest bug helper song drew only about 3.5K views in two and a half days.

Lili and Max (US, 1,637 videos of pretend play 'good habits' cartoons and recycled nursery rhyme compilations) fell from several hundred thousand views a month in early 2025 to about 10K to 23K a month since mid 2025 and loses about 1,000 subscribers a month; the drop coincides with YouTube's July 2025 inauthentic and repetitive content rules, a warning that mass produced, look alike uploads can lose almost all reach.

Lalafun spreads its songs across several English sister channels: Little Lalaby (US, since Jun 2023, 1.17M subscribers, 622M views, 1,833 videos) gained about 18.3M views in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 after a July peak of 46M a month, alongside Funlala (about 42M a month) and the 15M subscriber main channel, so a proven song brand can fill several channels and feeds at once.

Little Lalaby's 13 Nov 2026 upload 'A Ram Sam Sam, Move Your Hands and Feet!' (a public domain Moroccan folk action song) reached about 33K views in under three days, roughly 28 times its usual, and its third biggest video is an Aug 2026 'Don't Cry, Baby! Wheels on the Bus' newborn soothing song (1.45M), so action songs with hand and feet moves and baby soothing stories are this network's current winners.

Nursery Rhymes KS 3D (611K subscribers, 55M views) built its audience from only 76 very long compilations averaging nearly two hours and then stopped uploading; by mid 2025 it earned only a few thousand views a day and was losing subscribers, a sign that long compilations without a stream of fresh songs fade.

Monterey Bay Aquarium launched a YouTube Kids channel on 10 Nov 2026 with eight episodes on day one in five repeatable formats, including a calm one minute 'ocean wonder' of animals moving and an 'I spot' clue game where children find animals in the footage, a sign that trusted institutions now build kids channels around short, named, repeatable segments.

Blippi posted 12 videos in 1 to 13 Nov 2026, nine of them Shorts of 25 to 87 seconds and the long ones mostly two hour compilations, which confirms the leading kids brands now run about two thirds Shorts in their upload mix.

ChuChu TV's main channel slid from about 390 to 460M monthly views in 2025 to about 270 to 330M a month through 2026 (285.8M in October), roughly a 30% drop, while calmer Super Simple Songs grew about 17% over the same months, so older remix style rhyme libraries are losing ground to fresh, simple originals.

ChuChu TV's Diwali story Short (7 Nov 2026) drew only about 59K views in its first five and a half days on a 98M subscriber channel, a reminder that even giant channels get small Shorts reach for festival story Shorts without a song or dance hook.

Bebefinn Portuguese (9.08M subscribers, 7.74B views) gained about 150K subscribers and about 296M views in the 28 days to late October 2026 with roughly 20 uploads a month, showing a dubbed local language channel of a global character brand can grow faster than many English originals.

vidIQ's US top 100 by subscribers on 14 Nov 2026 holds about 34 kids and family channels, with three nursery rhyme music brands in the top 20 (CoComelon No. 2 at 203M, Pinkfong No. 11 at 85.4M, LooLoo Kids No. 18 at 62.8M), so music led preschool channels remain the strongest kids format on US YouTube.

Twin brothers Lucas and Marcus sit at No. 64 in the US top 100 (about 37.2M subscribers, 14 Nov 2026), and sibling duos (Vlad and Niki, Diana and Roma) dominate the family list, which supports a brothers duo as a brand that kids worldwide relate to.

BabyBus's main English channel (44.2M subscribers) gained about 2.56B views in January to October 2026 against about 2.95B a year earlier (about 13% lower, still about 220M a month in autumn), so even the second biggest preschool song brand is shrinking slightly as viewing spreads across more channels.

Little Angel and Friends gained only about 429M views in January to October 2026 against about 959M in the same months of 2025, more than halving outside one August spike, while it keeps uploading routine songs (a 'no no bath time' song on 14 Nov 2026), so a big back catalogue alone does not protect a nursery channel's reach.

Ms Rachel's YouTube channel (21.9M subscribers, about 318M views in the 28 days to 15 Nov 2026) gained about 4.12B views in January to October 2026 against about 3.92B a year earlier, one of the few big preschool channels still growing while CoComelon, ChuChu TV and Little Angel shrink.

Ms Rachel's 30 Oct 2026 upload 'Best Baby Songs ... Open Shut Them + More', a long compilation for babies, drew about 8.4M views in 15 days (an outlier over 100 times her normal), showing that a baby aimed (under 2) compilation with a hand action song in the title can still break out in late 2026.

Pinkfong's main channel (85.4M subscribers) gained about 4.72B views in January to October 2026, only about 3% below 2025 and about 426M in the 28 days to 15 Nov, so it is holding steady while ChuChu TV and Little Angel fall sharply.

Pinkfong's most watched video is not Baby Shark but 'Monkey Banana Dance' (Jun 2023, about 922M views, five times its next best), a simple animal dance along song, and its other top uploads are dance along compilations, which confirms a named animal plus a copyable dance is the strongest single song format.

Pinkfong's newest main channel upload (12 Nov 2026) is a vehicle rescue story ('The Super Rescue Team is Hurt') from its car mechanic spin off, about 173K views in two days, showing even song brands now mix in vehicle rescue stories to keep boys aged 2 to 5 watching.

Kids Diana Show gained about 5.0B views in January to October 2026 against about 10.6B in the same months of 2025, roughly half, with zero subscriber growth, even though it still packages videos as challenges, mazes and escape rooms; together with ChuChu TV and Little Angel this shows 2026 is shrinking the old giants while Ms Rachel, Super Simple Songs and Danny Go! grow.

The Kiboomers (about 4.05M subscribers, 4.6B lifetime views, 1,486 videos) built its brand on movement game songs such as Freeze Dance, Floor is Lava and Going on a Bear Hunt, the same stop and go dance space Bro Bros plays in.

The Kiboomers' new uploads in Sep to Nov 2026 are themed compilations (fall, Halloween, animal, movement) that average only about 115K lifetime views each, so its reach now comes from old evergreen hits rather than fresh uploads; new singles, not compilations, are what build a catalog.

Toy and kids channels that run several 24/7 streams can get most of their traffic from them: BIBO and Toys (12.4M subscribers, about 60 streams a month) drew 86% of traffic and 93% of revenue from streams, and Prenses MeLisa drew 93% of traffic from 4 to 8 streams while uploading less than once a month.
Translated channel networks keep paying off for kids brands: Amelka Karamelka's translated channels hold about 436M views and over 1M subscribers, alongside Lady Diana's 52 dubbed channels.

Hey Bear Sensory's views per upload have fallen steeply (about 61M for its first 10 videos, 17M for the next 10, 5.4M for the latest 10) yet the channel still earns about 51M views a month from just 95 videos and under one upload a month, because its early dancing fruit hits keep playing; one breakout dance format can carry a channel for years.

Hey Bear's newest uploads are short (mostly 1 to 6 minutes) while its biggest hits run 10 to 27 minutes, so its long, looping dance parties rather than its new short clips remain what children replay.

Big kids brands run holiday crossovers as paired uploads: Blippi and the Dr Seuss channel each posted a different episode on the same day (19 Dec 2025, gingerbread houses on one channel and Christmas games on the other) so each audience is sent to the other channel; small channels can copy the idea with a friendly creator, each posting its own version of one shared song.

A brand new German animated kids song channel (Bobo and Fibis Kinderwelt, about 5 weeks old, 2.8 uploads a week, about 2 minute songs) averages about 1,100 views per video with 195 subscribers, and its only breakout is a 'Mama, you are wonderful' family song, a realistic benchmark for a young channel like Bro Bros and a sign that songs about loving a parent stand out early.

Netflix Jr's YouTube channel (26.6M subscribers, 20B views) posts several clips a day in November 2026, mostly from its new show Doozie's Doghouse plus game style hooks ('Mystery Wheel of Doozie Dogs' 194K, 'Play Hide and Seek' 168K in under a week) that push kids to its Netflix Playground games app, so even streamers use short choose and find games on YouTube to pull children in.

An openly AI branded kids music channel ('AI Kids Songs', about 1,100 uploads since April 2024) has only about 24K subscribers and its October 2025 lullaby uploads drew 35 to 292 views each, more evidence that mass uploading generic AI songs does not build a kids audience.

Indonesian kids song channel NANANA KIDS (316K subscribers, 11,591 videos, mostly remixes and compilations) slid from about 3.2M monthly views in Feb 2026 to about 170K in Oct 2026 and gained no subscribers in the last 28 days, another sign that bulk compilation channels without fresh characters or stories are losing reach in 2026.

Bebefinn's first feature (streaming on Netflix from Apr 2026) has the youngest brother pulled into a tablet and his siblings teaming up with mascot friends to bring him home, with sing along numbers that hop between jazz, EDM and Broadway styles and scenes that switch from 3D to pixel art; a Bro Bros 'brother inside the video game' song with a pixel art verse and a style change per verse is the same trick on a small budget.
