Bebefinn's Korean language channel (5.14M subscribers, about 4.5B views) still drew about 65M views in the 28 days to 13 Nov 2026 with short role play songs such as fixing a toy car with hashtags in the title, showing that a big brand keeps a separate home language channel fed with pretend play songs alongside its English channel.

ChuChu TV, which says it has over 180M subscribers and 100B views across its channels, hired Cookbook Media (Sep 2025) to sell its library to TV and streaming and build toys, publishing, live shows and games in North America, so the largest Indian kids song brand is turning into a licensed lifestyle brand built on recurring characters, not just songs.

ChuChu TV's main channel (98.2M subscribers, about 61B views) gained about 391M views in Dec 2025 but only about 286M in Oct 2026 with flat subscribers, and its newest upload (13 Nov 2026) is a 24 minute themed story compilation ('Curiosity Corner') with about 32K views in under three days, so even a giant now earns mostly from old remixed classics while new uploads start small.

Little Angel's main English channel (7.3M subscribers) swings wildly month to month (about 125M views in Aug 2026, 14M in Sep, 26M in Oct) and showed no December lift in either of the last two years (52M in Dec 2024, 39M in Dec 2025), so for a nursery song channel Christmas songs add seasonal search traffic but do not reliably lift the whole channel; our winter plan should mix evergreen routine songs with the holiday ones.

Little Angel's newest upload on 14 Nov 2026 is a bath time 'no no' routine song (about 17K views in 10 hours), showing the biggest nursery brands keep returning to everyday care routines (bath, bedtime, boo boos) even in mid November rather than switching fully to Christmas.

Bebefinn's Korean language channel peaked at about 467M views in November 2025 and slid to about 69M in October 2026 (around 85% lower) while still uploading most days, so even a mega brand's single language channel can fade fast once its early hits age; growth has to come from fresh hit songs and new language tracks, not volume alone.

Hey Bear Sensory's best recent upload is a 'Party Time Dance Off!' (about 3.9M views in two months, ahead of its Halloween party at 2.7M), so even an older dance brand gets its strongest new response from a simple dance battle between friendly characters, a format the Bros can copy with their own song.

The Wiggles (11M subscribers, about 6.26B views, 1,483 videos) upload about one short song a day (1 to 3.5 minutes) with a median of about 54K views, yet a farm animal remake of Wheels on the Bus (15 Oct 2026) passed 3.7M in under three weeks while new originals sat at 8K to 30K, so classic rhyme remakes still carry daily uploaders.

The Wiggles remake their own hits in a new genre ('Bouncing Balls, Country Music Version', 343K views in under two weeks, far above their median) and title songs as name, emoji, brand, then a plain descriptor ('Fun Animal Song for Kids', 'Nursery Rhyme'), so a country, reggae or rock version of a Bro Bros hit is a cheap second upload.

The Wiggles released 20 studio albums in one year under a global Universal Music deal and say their YouTube audience is growing in Germany, Italy and France, with plans to take the catalogue into more languages (they already run Los Wiggles for Latin America), so European languages are rising for English preschool music too.

YUM YUM Kids Songs (US, since May 2023, 1.25M subscribers, 590M views from 573 videos) grew on one repeatable concept: 'School Bus Lost Wheel' (143.5M views) then the same story with an ambulance (27.1M) and an excavator (25.9M), so one strong problem story can be re run with new vehicles or animals as a Bro Bros series.

YUM YUM's best month of 2026 was October (35.8M views against 15M to 24M in other months) even though its last upload was a Halloween bus remix on 30 Sep, showing that a seasonal version of a proven hit posted a month early keeps earning through the whole season without new uploads.

Farmees (9.87M subscribers, 3.34B views, 1,896 videos) has had no subscriber change in 28 days and its newest uploads (Christmas Shorts, 28 minute dance compilations, rhyme Shorts stuffed with #trending #viral tags) draw only about 4K to 28K views each, a warning that hashtag stuffing and recycled rhymes no longer lift a large channel.

Baby Zoo (US, 10.7M subscribers, 10.3B views) got its biggest hits from tiny toddler problems sung as a song: 'Mommy I Can't Sleep' (195M), 'Where Is My Mouth' (117M), 'Bottle Feeding' (106M) and 'No It's Too Hot' (101M), each a small worry solved by a parent, so a 'little problem, kind fix' song shape is proven.

Baby Zoo's monthly views slid from about 100M in Jan 2026 to about 29M in Oct 2026 with subscribers flat at 10.7M for a year, and its 31 Oct 2026 upload had only 51K views after four days, so even big remix style song channels are losing reach in 2026 while fresher formats grow.

Baby Zoo titles every hit as 'Song name + emoji | + More Best Kids Songs and Nursery Rhymes by Baby Zoo', meaning the top videos are compilations led by one hit song, which supports our plan of a weekly mix titled after the strongest single.

Kids Learning Songs (US, since 2010, 10.5M subscribers) earns a steady 16M to 25M views a month in 2026 from colour songs (75M top video), Head Shoulders Knees and Toes and health routines such as brushing teeth and visiting the dentist, so hygiene and body songs remain reliable evergreen earners.

Kids Learning Songs posts only about once a week yet its 3 Aug 2026 school prep video passed 395K views, showing that a slower cadence with clear routine topics can still reach viewers when the channel has years of watch history.

Farmees (9.87M subscribers) posted 48 uploads between 3 Aug and 17 Nov 2026 (30 long, 18 Shorts) with a median gap of 2 days and median views of about 19K; its 16 Nov 'Christmas Wheels on the Bus' remake (1:41) had 13.5K views after two days, while a September ABC song is its best at about 288K, so even a 10M channel's seasonal remakes start slowly.

CocoBus Nursery Rhymes published about 109 videos in the last 28 days (3,145 in total since Aug 2024) and still has only about 10.8K subscribers, with views sliding from about 359K in May 2026 to 245K in October; its newest mash up got about 1K views in 13 hours, fresh proof that volume alone does not grow a kids channel.

Rhythm And Nursery Rhymes Time For Kids (US, joined Aug 2022) has about 815K subscribers and 350M views from 818 videos, roughly 430K views per video, showing a mid size song channel can still break through within four years.

Kikoo Club (India, joined Jul 2023) reached about 808K subscribers and 969M views from only 330 videos, but its most viewed long video (a Baa Baa Black Sheep colours lullaby) has about 493K views, so almost all of its views came from Shorts; vidIQ models only a few dollars of ad income, a warning that a Shorts only audience pays almost nothing.

Kikoo Club's monthly views fell from about 14M in Feb and Apr 2026 to about 2.7M in Oct while subscribers sat flat around 808K and even dipped, and its newest dump truck song (24 Oct) got about 3.5K views in a day, so a Shorts boom fades within months unless long songs build a library.

Kikoo Club's second biggest long video is 'Laxman Chacha had a farm', an Indian adaptation of Old MacDonald (268K views), showing a local name swap inside a familiar song structure works for Indian audiences; for Bro Bros the same idea means original songs with local name and food swaps in dubbed versions.

Dave and Ava (15.9M) uploaded 20 videos in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 with zero subscriber gain, and its newest, 'The Wheels on the Bus Part 2 - Animal Song' (16 Nov), had about 17K views after a day and a half, again showing 'Part 2' remakes of classics start slowly for legacy 3D channels.

Nine of ChuChu TV's 15 newest uploads (25 Jul to 8 Oct 2026) went out on a Friday, with a few on Thursdays and Saturdays, and every long one puts its runtime in the title ('57 Min', '19 Min'), the same Friday compilation habit our playbook already follows.

Among those uploads ChuChu's 'Learn Numbers 1 to 10 with Surprise Eggs' hour led with about 858K views and 'Dinosaur Songs for Kids' (30 min) had about 620K, while its newer 'Bestie and Friends' story skits got about 30K to 305K and 'How to Draw' hours 25K to 346K, so learning plus surprise reveals still beat new story formats for a song brand.

ChuChu TV had posted no Christmas themed upload on its main channel by mid November 2026 and no Shorts in its last 15 uploads, so the biggest Indian kids brand leaves the late November Christmas window on main YouTube open for smaller channels.

YouTube's Creator Premieres event in Los Angeles (17 Nov 2026) showed a slate of creator series aimed at advertisers and TV, but none of it was for kids or families, unlike last year's event that featured Ms Rachel.

Mundo Canticuentos (Colombia, since 2014) has 9.47M subscribers, 5.45B views and 1,153 videos and still gains about 40 to 55M views a month in 2026, although new subscribers slowed from 110K in Dec 2025 to 20K to 30K a month.

Mundo Canticuentos' biggest video is a vowels remix (589M views), and its next two are versions of a popular Latin American Christmas donkey song (109M from Dec 2024 and 89M from Dec 2021), so a learning remix and a December song are its two strongest engines.
Mundo Canticuentos' 'I am a cup' object song (Jun 2025, 32M views) shows that a song where kids become an everyday object with one pose per line (handle, spout, pour) travels well in Latin America.

Mundo Canticuentos already posted its Christmas Short on 11 Nov 2026 (a Jingle Bells Short, about 7K views in 18 hours), a sign Latin American kids channels start their Christmas uploads by mid November.

Lellobee en Español Latino (Mexico, 802K subscribers, 264M views, 1,022 videos) last uploaded on 13 Dec 2025 and gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 2 Nov 2026, with views falling from about 0.9 to 1.2M a month early in 2026 to about 0.5M in Oct.

Lellobee's best Spanish videos have only about 125K to 221K views each despite 1,000+ uploads, so a big dubbed catalogue alone does not create hits; the Spanish market rewards a few strong songs promoted well.

Cocobi's English channel (US, since Feb 2021) has 3.36M subscribers and 2.96B views from 2,362 videos, and its monthly views roughly doubled in 2026 (about 54M in Jan to 116M in Oct, then 131M in the 28 days to 18 Nov) while it posted about 51 videos in four weeks.

Cocobi English's five most viewed long videos are a 'baby is born' story song (33M), a stranger danger safety song (32.7M), 'Escape from the colour prison' (29M), a 'what is a parasite' science song (28M) and an elevator safety compilation (23.6M), so safety and surprising science topics carry this Korean brand's biggest hits.
Cocobi's newest upload on 17 Nov 2026 is a 'Baby turned into a giant!' Short (about 34K views in 9 hours), using the same sudden size change surprise that works in kids Shorts generally.

Hogi and Pinkfong (16.7M subscribers, 18 Nov 2026) slipped from about 365M monthly views in May 2026 to about 264M in October on roughly 21 uploads a month, and all five of its most viewed videos are colour learning songs built around one satisfying object (a colourful pop it 308M, a candy machine 138M, a Halloween monster candy shop 125M, a dino special 95M, a boo boo song 91M).

Kids Diana Show's main channel (138M) drew about 454M views in October 2026, up from 387M in September, and its newest upload on 17 Nov is 'Adam and Oliver's Adventure Collection', a compilation led by the younger brothers rather than Diana, showing the brand passing its lead to the next sibling pair and leaning on compilations.

Tubefilter's most viewed chart for 9 to 15 Nov 2026 has 42 of 50 channels mainly on Shorts and 24 of 50 from India (US 8, Canada 3); a family Shorts channel, Fitu K Kitu, went to #1 with about 1.2B weekly views (+138%), nearly two thirds of its lifetime traffic in a single week, so one breakout Shorts format can multiply a channel in days.

In the same week no classic nursery song brand (CoComelon, Pinkfong, ChuChu, BabyBus, Super Simple) made the most viewed top 50, while kid friendly Shorts families and animation (Koko and Golu #17 at 509M, Keizo and Friends #22 at 444M) did, and the kids clown channel El Payaso Plim Plim has not dropped below 250M weekly views in six months; short, character led comedy now out views long nursery songs on reach.

Little Angel's 7.3M 'Nursery Rhymes and Kids Songs' channel gained almost no subscribers in 2026 (0 to 10K a month against 100K to 120K in mid 2025) while monthly views swung from 14M (Sep) to 125M (Aug) and 26M (Oct), showing that a single viral month does not carry over and that steady weekly hits matter more than one spike.

Little Angel's newest uploads (15 to 17 Nov 2026) are about one a day: a counting Short led by a helper job character ('Can You Count with Firefighter Jill?', about 2.1 times its usual early views) and a funny dad themed ballet story ('My Daddy Is the Best!'), so the old giants now lean on Shorts that mix a job hero or a family member with a simple learning task.

The fastest growing channel in Tubefilter's week of 15 Nov 2026, Chispita (Uruguay, Spanish), added about 770K subscribers in seven days and about 117M views in 28 days from only 124 videos, using dramatic skit Shorts with shouty all caps titles (a bully, a teacher who poisoned the class, a kidnapped sister); such shock drama spreads fast in Spanish speaking feeds but would break kids quality rules, so we take only the lesson that strong one line story hooks win, told gently.

BabyBus's English channel (44.2M, 18 Nov 2026) still adds about 100K subscribers a month on about 22 uploads per four weeks, but monthly views slid from about 257M in June to 218M in October 2026; its newest upload is a car safety rules story ('The Missing Cable Car', Sheriff Labrador), confirming that safety stories with a hero character are the brand's current push.

The Christmas Songs and Carols (Love to Sing) channel, 3.03M subscribers and 1.79B views, gained about 9.4M views from 19 Sep to 18 Oct 2026 (roughly 300K a day) and uploaded its 2026 Christmas playlist on 17 Oct, so holiday song demand starts building from mid October and our own winter songs should be live by late November to ride December.

That carol channel's top videos are simple lyrics on screen versions (Feliz Navidad with lyrics 18.8M, Jingle Bells with lyrics 10.4M, Deck the Halls 9.5M) and a 'Top 90 Christmas Songs' compilation (14.6M), so a lyrics on screen sing along cut of each original Bro Bros winter song is a cheap extra upload that families search for at parties.

RhymeMusicBox (276K subscribers, 178M views from only 44 videos) owes 128M views to one Baby Shark plus Ten in the Bed medley, posted nothing new after Oct 2024, and showed net monthly view losses in Aug (minus 4.0M) and Oct 2026 (minus 2.5M), likely view count corrections, so a channel that leans on one public domain medley stalls without fresh uploads.

Kids Song Family shows 7.77M subscribers but only about 8.6K total views on 12 videos and now posts toddler songs that name famous characters in titles, a sign of a repurposed old channel, so subscriber counts alone are a poor guide to which kids competitors really matter; views per video and recent monthly views are the better yardstick.

Dave and Ava (15.9M subscribers, 12.8B views, 3D nursery rhymes) still earns about 1.7M views a day; its monthly views ran 37M to 57M over the last year with peaks in May (57M) and August (54M), the long school holiday months, rather than December, so summer is as big a season for 3D nursery channels as Christmas.

Dave and Ava posted about 20 videos in the last 28 days and its newest (16 Nov 2026) is a 'Part 2' animal version of a classic bus song (17K views in 34 hours), while its all time top videos are Halloween and monster sing alongs (11.9M and 7.5M), so sequels of a known song with a new twist and spooky friendly monster songs are its proven formats.

Mother Goose Club (9.89M, live action costumed rhymes) fell from about 30.2M views in Nov 2025 to 21.0M in Oct 2026 (about minus 30%) while posting only 6 videos in 28 days, and its newest upload, a Thanksgiving greeting, had about 20K views after five days, so a slow upload rhythm and greeting style uploads let even a big catalogue channel shrink.

Mother Goose Club's best videos are all '+ More' compilations led by one learning anchor (ABC Song + More 4.4M, Phonics Song 1.7M), the same compilation naming pattern as the biggest nursery channels, confirming that a famous lead song plus 'and more' is the standard title for long kids compilations.

FunForKidsTV (US, 3.12M subscribers, 2.37B views) gained 20K subscribers in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 from 9 uploads, but its monthly views swing wildly: about 25M to 50M in a normal month, 78M in August and 455M in February 2026, so one breakout month can bring as many views as a whole normal year for a mid sized nursery channel.

FunForKidsTV's biggest videos are 'got a boo boo' care songs about a hurt baby animal being helped (142M and 43M) and a 'strongest dinosaur' song (33M), and its newest Short (14 Nov 2026, about 26K views in 3 days) asks 'Can you guess which shape is the best dancer?', a quiz plus dance hook we can copy with our own shape friends.

Zoobees (US, 179K subscribers, about 1M views a month) posted a Christmas finger play song with Santa on 12 Nov 2026 that had only about 2K views after five days while its 2023 bus and finger family videos still carry the channel, so an early Christmas upload from a small channel will not pop on its own; it needs a strong hook song and time to be found in December.

Kids Learn and Grow (US, 882K subscribers, 669M views since Dec 2022) earns a remarkably flat 17M to 24M views every month with no December spike and adds about 20K subscribers a month, so toddler learning videos (counting, shapes, colours) are evergreen demand that keeps paying all year while holiday songs come and go.

That channel's top videos use plain search phrase titles that list every skill ('Toddler Learning Videos | Kids Learn to Count, Shapes & Colors', 126M views; 'Counting & Numbers Educational Videos for Toddlers', 28.9M), and it re made its best title in Dec 2025 (22M views), so remaking a proven learning video with the same search title is a valid strategy; our counting and colour songs should list the skills in the title.

An Indian channel showing 2.38M subscribers has only about 2.1M lifetime views on 41 videos, another sign that bought or repurposed channels inflate subscriber charts, so when we benchmark competitors we use monthly views and views per video, never subscribers.

Super Simple Songs (47.3M subscribers, 65B views) reached its best month of the past year in October 2026 (about 592M views, up from about 478M in Nov 2025) and added about 200K subscribers in 28 days while uploading only 4 videos, so a deep catalogue of calm, teacher friendly songs keeps compounding even with a slow upload rhythm.

Super Simple Songs' newest song, a silly worded hand and face washing song posted 5 Nov 2026, had about 1.54M views after 12 days (about 8.7K views an hour, 2.8 times the channel's usual), so daily routine songs (washing, brushing, tidying) with a playful made up word in the title are still a winning formula for the biggest preschool brand.

HeyKids English (4.78M subscribers, 2.83B views) earns about 17M to 27M views a month, with a March 2026 high of 44M, and its top videos are a construction vehicles song (79.7M), a Halloween song (64.5M) and a train song (51.6M), so vehicles plus one seasonal anthem a year are the backbone of a mid sized 3D nursery channel.

HeyKids turned one public domain action song into a family of versions (a Christmas edition, 27.4M views, and a birthday edition, 26.8M), showing that a single simple chant re dressed for each occasion keeps earning; we can do the same with one original Bro Bros action chant reused for Christmas, birthdays and New Year.

Kids Channel Preschool (US, 826K) gets about 343M of its 511M lifetime views from one 2022 phonics song, and its views rise in May and June (about 9M a month) and fall to about 4M to 5M in winter, while its new Santa song had only 348 views in two days, so a small channel's Christmas song without search demand or a hook rarely moves, and evergreen learning songs carry the year.

RhymeMusicBox (US, 276K subscribers) has 178M views from only 44 videos and nothing new since October 2024, and one pairing video, 'Baby Shark + Ten in the Bed' (Mar 2024), alone holds about 128M views while it still pulls about 12,600 views a day, so a single two song pairing can carry a small channel for years.

That same channel's other top videos are all two song pairings joined with a plus sign or 'and' ('Ten in the Bed and Johny Johny Yes Papa' 20.8M, 'Wheels on the Bus and Baa Baa Black Sheep' 5.5M, 'Wheels on the Bus + Vehicles Song' 2.1M), which supports titling Bro Bros mini compilations as 'Song A + Song B' using our two strongest originals.

In Tubefilter's most subscribed chart for 9 to 15 Nov 2026, 36 of the top 50 weekly gainers are mainly Shorts channels, so Shorts remain the main subscriber engine and every Bro Bros song should ship with at least one Short.

Alan's Universe gained about 1M YouTube subscribers in one week and rose to fourth in Tubefilter's chart right after its Netflix debut, which suggests a show landing on a streamer feeds subscribers back to its YouTube channel.

The Kiboomers (Canada, about 4.05M subscribers, 4.6B views, 1,486 videos) still pull about 45M views in 28 days while posting only about 5 new videos a month on a stated 'new video every Friday' schedule, so a deep back catalogue of movement songs keeps earning long after upload.

The Kiboomers built a whole family of freeze dance songs (party, animal, spring and other seasonal versions) that teachers use as circle time and brain break songs; one proven game format re-made for every season is a cheap way for Bro Bros to grow a series.
leaves.src: vidIQ and Kiboomers channel listings, Nov 2026

leaves.t: The Kiboomers say they also have over 1 billion streams on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon, so a small team of movement songs can earn on audio platforms too; uploading our Suno songs to streaming services is worth testing.

Tiny Tunes (UK, about 872K subscribers) has about 1.2B views from only 112 videos, roughly 10M views per video, on phonics, times tables, alphabet and counting songs, proof that a few polished evergreen learning songs can beat volume.

In Tubefilter's most viewed chart for 2 to 8 Nov 2026, about a dozen kids and family channels sit in the top 50, led by Cadel and Mia (890M weekly views even after a 24% drop) and two Sierra and Rhia channels (742M and 705M), so family skit Shorts still dominate global kids viewing.

The Spanish language preschool channel El Tren Nam Nam fell 52% in one week (from 7th to 39th, about 360M weekly views) in early November 2026, a sign that huge Shorts driven kids channels can swing sharply week to week.

GoBooBoo (US, 4.29M subscribers) has 2.27B views from only 197 videos; one finger family style video holds 930M, and its 'Boo Boo Song + Wheels on the Ambulance' pairing holds about 150M, showing that a familiar boo boo theme paired with a vehicle song is a proven combination.

GoBooBoo's newest upload (a boo boo song, 12 Nov 2026) had only about 39K views after almost two days while the channel earns about 36M views in 28 days, so even big nursery channels live on their back catalogue and new songs build slowly.

GoBooBoo's second biggest video is a gentle 'something in the dark' song (194M views), so a soft not scary 'who is in the dark?' song with a friendly reveal is a proven kids topic; our shy fluffy monster bedtime song fits it.

Kids Channel India's separate Shorts channel (3D nursery rhymes) has about 375K subscribers and 118M views from 478 Shorts since 2021, roughly 250K views per Short, a realistic benchmark for an Indian 3D rhymes Shorts channel.

Lalafun's main channel (US, 15.2M subscribers, 11.65B views) gained about 500K subscribers and 592M views in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 from only 13 uploads, about three a week, so heavy reach comes from strong songs and Shorts, not from posting many long videos.

Lalafun grew only 0 to 100K subscribers a month in early 2026 but 600K to 700K a month from May to October 2026, showing a kids channel can break out suddenly after months of slow growth once a few Shorts hit.

ChuChu TV's main channel (98.2M subscribers, 61B views) gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 yet still earns about 223M views a month from its back catalogue, and its newest upload is a 24 minute story compilation ('Curiosity Corner'), so the old giants now lean on long compilations.

ChuChu TV's top five videos of all time are 2021 to 2022 'Classics' with surprise egg animal and vehicle reveals (up to 194M views), so the 'what is inside?' reveal game is a lasting preschool hook that Bro Bros can use with our own original eggs, boxes or presents.

ChuChu TV's learning channel Jumblikans (India, 5.42M) still draws about 39M views a month mostly from 2022 rhymes, but its newest video (4 Oct 2026, a healthy food rhyme) had only about 247K views after a month, another sign that new uploads on older kids channels grow slowly.

In the same week last year (17 to 23 Nov 2025), most kids Shorts channels in Tubefilter's top 50 lost views (Toys and Colors minus 14%, Kidshire minus 20%, Kids Land minus 24%, Billy Blip Boss minus 25%) while family skit channel Cadel and Mia rose 12% to about 1.04B, so a late November dip in generic kids Shorts is seasonal, not a sign of failure.

A baby focused Shorts channel, BabyBillion, held steady at about 600M weekly views in the week before US Thanksgiving 2025 while other kids channels fell, suggesting baby and toddler content is less affected by holiday schedule changes than older kids content.

Bebefinn's Spanish channel (18.2M subscribers) earned about 453M views in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026, more than its English main channel (37.3M subscribers, about 378M), so a Spanish version of a song brand can out earn the English original in views.

Bebefinn Spanish has held a steady 444M to 494M views every month from May to October 2026 with about 200K new subscribers a month, showing how stable a well fed Spanish preschool catalogue is compared with fast swinging English Shorts channels.

Bebefinn's newest songs are numbered episodes tied to a child's wish or a party ('I Want to Be a Ballerina!' EP222, 'The Pinata Song' EP200 in Spanish), and the English one reached about 247K views in 37 hours, so numbered episode branding plus a dream job or party theme keeps a song series feeling like a show.

Bebefinn's all time top video is still its 2022 'Good Morning' wake up song (about 775M views), ahead of its Baby Shark crossover, so a morning routine song with a named character waking up is one of the most durable preschool song formats.

CoComelon's Portuguese channel (Brazil, 4.45M subscribers) earned about 87M views in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026, but the 19 videos it published in that time brought only about 2.4M of them, so roughly 97% of a mature kids channel's views come from its back catalogue.

CoComelon Portuguese's 7 new Shorts in late October to mid November 2026 earned only about 189K views combined, far below its long videos, while its best Short ever ('DIY 1-2-3', Jan 2025) holds 130M, so Shorts hits are rare spikes and most Shorts from big brands now land quietly.

Jason Vlogs' team advises starting with one Short a day and scaling to 5 to 10 a day once a rhythm is set, but says Shorts bring reach rather than revenue and long videos and compilations still earn far higher CPMs, matching our plan of two long songs a day each with its Short.
leaves.src: AIR Media-Tech interview with Jason Vlogs

leaves.t: Kids Diana Show (138M subscribers) added no subscribers in any month of 2026 yet still earns about 380M to 545M views a month from 1,771 videos, and its only recent subscriber jump came in December 2025 (+1M), another sign that December is the strongest growth month for kids channels.

Kids Diana Show's five biggest videos are a safety rules story (school bus rules, 566M) and challenge adventures (escape room 505M, 'open the 10 doors' 443M, a maze to help the baby brother 431M), so 'choose a door' and 'get through the maze to help Little Bro' song games are proven kid hooks we can make with our own songs.

Kids Diana Show's newest upload (17 Nov 2026) is a collection with a younger brother pair as leads ('Adam and Oliver's Adventure Collection') and drew about 40K views in 12 hours, so even the biggest kids brand now leans on compilations and brother characters.

Miliki Family (2.59M subscribers, 1.57B views, only 498 videos) is built on 'afraid of' songs: its top video, a child who cannot sleep because of the dark, has 381M views, and two more of its top five are about fear of a shot at the doctor (36M) and of the dentist (33M).

Miliki Family roughly doubled its monthly views from about 20M in June 2026 to 46M in September and 40M in October while posting only about 14 videos a month, so a strong theme library can grow without a flood of uploads.

Mike and Mia (1.66M subscribers, 755 videos since 2016) has gained no subscribers for six months and draws only about 1.8M views a month; its best videos are habit songs (haircut 9.9M, boo boo 6.9M), showing that an older catalog slowly fades without a new breakout theme.

Even established kids channels start slowly: Miliki Family's newest fire truck song had 938 views and Mike and Mia's newest phonics song 570 views in their first 11 hours, so a Bro Bros upload with a few hundred views on day one is normal and should be judged after a week or more.

Little Treehouse Toddler Fun Learning (547K subscribers, 304M views) owes its two biggest videos to Christmas songs posted in mid and late November 2023 (36.5M and 28.3M views), more than any of its colours, ABC or shapes songs, so a Christmas song posted in the second half of November can become a channel's top video for years.

Little Treehouse posted its 2026 Christmas song ('ABC Hip Hop Alphabet Christmas') on 16 Nov and it had only about 800 views after 34 hours, which fits the pattern that holiday songs start slowly and peak in December searches.

Little Treehouse Toddler Fun Learning grows steadily at about 4K to 6K subscribers and 5M to 7.5M views a month with mostly learning songs, showing a mid size preschool channel can stay healthy without trends, on evergreen colours, shapes, ABC and seasonal songs.

Super Simple Songs (70M+ subscribers) released its 2026 original songs on Thursdays, one every two weeks (19 from 8 Jan to 24 Sep), so the most trusted preschool brand grows on a slow, steady calendar of carefully made songs rather than daily volume.

In Tubefilter's 9 to 15 Nov 2026 chart, family Shorts duos still hold the top: Sierra and Rhia English (#4, about 730M weekly views), Cadel and Mia (#6, 693M, down 22%) and Sierra and Rhia FAM (#7, 626M), so pairs of characters with simple everyday sibling or parent stories remain the strongest Shorts formula.

New in the same week's top 50: Twin Twin (US, #40, about 331M weekly views) and Indonesia's Nabel Dan Mama (#49, about 302M), a mother and child duo, while Canada's Diary of 4 climbed nine places (+16%); twins and parent plus child pairs keep breaking in, which favours our two brothers as a fixed duo in every Short.

Moonbug's compilation only side channel 'Kids Road Trip!' (875K subscribers, about 1,010 videos averaging 52 minutes, about 3 uploads a week) drew only about 1.3M views a month (around 1,300 views per video) in early 2025, so a separate compilation channel is a weak use of effort compared with posting compilations on the main channel.

Tubefilter's most subscribed chart for 9 to 15 Nov 2026 is led by Latin American and Turkish creators: two Brazilian channels (+2M and +1M a week), Mexico's HotSpanish Vlogs (+1.5M) and Turkey's Sasha Show (+1.2M), so Portuguese and Spanish speaking audiences are where weekly subscriber growth is fastest right now.

A Singapore animation channel built on original cartoon characters in short battle stories (RABBITWARREN, 'Ninja Skunks vs. Oniball') made the same week's top 50 gainers with about 300K new subscribers (+50%), proof that original animated characters can grow fast on Shorts without any real people on screen.

Lalafun's German channel (2.76M subscribers, 2.35B views, 2,903 videos since May 2022) drew about 203M views in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 and gained 90K subscribers, so a dubbed German version of a 3D nursery rhyme brand can become a top channel on its own.

Lalafun's German top videos are sleepy baby versions of public domain rhymes (a Ten in the Bed bedtime medley 254M, Itsy Bitsy Spider newborn version 156M) and in 2026 new bus songs (Picnic Bus 43.6M, Family Bus 42.6M), so bedtime and bus themes travel well into German.

NuNu Tv Nursery Rhymes (US, 29.9M subscribers) has 26.7B views from only 847 videos (about 31M views per video) and still adds about 480M to 720M views a month (peaking at 722M in August 2026), proof that fewer, carefully made rhyme videos can out earn mass uploading.

NuNu Tv's top five mix colour twists on classic rhymes (Finger Family colours 325M, Baa Baa Color Sheep 272M), an animal version of Wheels on the Bus (303M) and two behaviour songs, 'I Want That, Share It Please' (270M) and a toddler activity song (232M), all posted 2024 to 2025, so sharing and turn taking songs can match the classics.

Pudding TV Nursery Rhymes (Norway, English songs, 197K subscribers, 231 videos since 2015) earns a flat 600K to 720K views a month and has not posted since Aug 2026; one Old MacDonald video (4.8M) dwarfs all others (under 400K each), a benchmark of how a small rhyme channel stalls without regular uploads or a repeatable hit format.

Kids smile TV (16.4M subscribers, about 9.8B views) now posts irregular 6 to 14 second Shorts built on borrowed characters such as Wednesday and Barbie and gets only about 20K to 54K views each (Nov 2026), while its 28 to 30 minute school story episodes reach about 300K to 370K, a sign that big old subscriber counts and borrowed characters do not keep Shorts reach alive.

Schoolies (US 3D nursery rhyme channel, 1.21M subscribers, about 738M views, 822 videos) slid from about 6M views in February 2026 to about 1.4M a month since, with flat subscribers, and its newest costume rhyme (16 Nov) had about 1.5K views after a day and a half, another sign that remade classic rhymes alone no longer win new reach.

Schoolies' best videos are original funny or playful songs rather than classics: a gentle spooky chase song for babies (77M), a Halloween teacher medley (21M) and two 'Oopsie Doopsie' silly dance songs (23M and 18M), which again shows that an original catchy nonsense word chorus with a funny dance outperforms a channel's remade rhymes.

About 32 of the 100 biggest US registered YouTube channels (vidIQ, 18 Nov 2026) are kids and family channels, led by CoComelon (203M), Vlad and Niki (151M), Kids Diana Show (138M) and Like Nastya (134M), with nursery rhyme brands Pinkfong (85M), LooLoo Kids (63M), BabyBus (44M), Little Baby Bum (42M) and Bebefinn (37M) further down.

Channel Crawler's May 2026 list of fastest growing US education channels put CoComelon second (+1M subscribers in 30 days) and included a children's crafts and manners channel, SparkleToon (+400K), that posted 137 videos in one month, and 9 of the 10 fastest growers relied mainly on Shorts.

Pinkfong released a Baby Shark collaboration song with Thailand's viral Butterbear mascot in English first and in Thai two weeks later, then ran a one month social dance challenge on it, a template for entering a market: partner with a loved local mascot, stagger the local language version, and attach a dance challenge.

Pinkfong's newer dinosaur series Dinolings reached 1M subscribers and 160M views by May 2026 with Season 2 views up 639% on Season 1, and a Spanish channel was planned next, showing that a second season of a focused theme can multiply views and that Spanish is the first add on language even for a Korean studio.

Baby Shark still draws about 400,000 Spotify streams a day worldwide (over 1B in total), proof that one kids hit keeps paying on audio platforms for years, so Bro Bros songs should also go out to Spotify and Apple Music.

In Nov 2026 Pinkfong described Japan as its growth base: a Bebefinn music pad hit number 1 in Amazon Japan's music toy category, Baby Shark themed hotel rooms opened in Chiba, and Christmas pop up stores with about 50 new products were set for Tokyo (4 Dec) and Osaka (11 Dec).

CoComelon Playdates with Sanrio Friends launched on a dedicated YouTube channel on 24 Jan 2026 with one 3 minute episode every Saturday, in a softer 2D pastel style than the main 3D show, mixing five Japanese nursery rhymes with a J pop flavoured remake, so even the biggest brand builds a separate channel, a fixed weekly slot and a regional music flavour for a new audience.

Moonbug released four songs from that crossover on music streaming a day before the first episode, a simple release order Bro Bros can copy: song on Spotify and Apple Music first, video the next day, so early listeners become the first viewers.

D Billions, a kids music brand with roots in Kyrgyzstan, reached about 56M subscribers and 55B YouTube views in five years (by Jun 2024) from 500+ original songs, four of them past a billion views, in 12 languages with an 80+ person team, proof that a small country studio can win worldwide with original songs, dances and a set of colourful characters.

D Billions moved from live performers in costumes to 2D and 3D animated storytelling while keeping original music, dances and activities at the centre, the same building blocks Bro Bros uses, and it frames every song as helping kids learn English or their own language.

Jack Hartmann, whose catchy, goofy learning songs are played in US classrooms, said his YouTube views 'exploded' after he moved from filmed performances to animation, his first year earned only about 400 USD, and YouTube assigned him a partner consultant at 100K subscribers, a reminder that teachers are a second audience for learning songs and that growth starts slowly.

The same review notes healthcare, education technology, toy and food brands investing in their own original animated characters as long term assets, a possible future sponsor or licensing route for an established Bro Bros cast (always outside made for kids ad limits and clearly labelled).

Booba began as a 3 minute wordless YouTube cartoon and its makers stretched episodes step by step to 5 and then 7 minutes while the audience kept growing, reaching about 22B views and 20M subscribers, a model for growing Bro Bros song videos in length only gradually and testing each step.
leaves.src: Kedoo and European Animation Journal, Mar and Dec 2025

leaves.t: Kedoo's rule for Booba is 'take what kids love and multiply it': themed versions of the same hero (a prehistoric one with a pet dinosaur, a bandit one on a hobby horse, a genie one) keep the familiar character in new worlds, so Bro Bros can run themed versions of the brothers (dino Bros, space Bros, chef Bros) without inventing new casts.

For its sixth season (26 episodes of 7 minutes, Disney+ from early 2026) Booba added Loola, a female lead, for better gender balance and Tiny Booba, a smaller cuter version meant to appeal especially to Asian markets, which supports giving Bro Bros a girl friend who leads some songs and a baby sized sidekick.

Kedoo says Booba stories are always told from the hero's point of view (what he wants and how he gets it), made by a small core team, and released so kids can watch whenever they like rather than on a timetable, which matches our plan of one clear wish per Bro Bros song.

After Moonbug refreshed Little Baby Bum's look and built a new curriculum with the education non profit Peeple (2022 to 2023), views of its new YouTube content grew about 30% month on month and the brand passed 95M subscribers across its channels, so a planned visual upgrade plus a named learning goal per song is worth doing once Bro Bros has a catalogue.

The kids long videos in the same weekly top 25 are all old evergreen classics (Wheels on the Bus +32.4M, Baby Shark Dance +22.9M, a baby first words video +13M, Baby Shark again +8.6M), so new long songs win slowly through search and Home while new Shorts can hit the weekly top 10 within days.

Kidshire's 'Winter Clothes for Kids' picture word Short added another 51.5M views in the week to 18 Nov 2026 after about 54.6M the week before, so a simple winter vocabulary Short keeps climbing through November, a strong case for a Bro Bros winter clothes dance Short now.

Two mid size toddler learning channels show the plateau many kids channels hit: Mayta the Brown Bear (198K subscribers, 156 videos) drew about 1.1M views in the 28 days to 6 Jan 2026 and Boey Bear (UK, 217K, 317 videos) about 0.85M in mid 2026 with only about 2K new subscribers, so steady new uploads matter more than catalogue size.

Mayta the Brown Bear's daily views fell from over 100K in Aug and Sep 2025 to about 16K to 50K in December but jumped to about 105K on Christmas Day, a sign that new tablets and TV time on 25 Dec briefly lift toddler channels, so a strong Bro Bros upload and a long compilation should be live before 25 Dec.

A 3D nursery rhyme channel that posted only 28 long videos (about 31 minutes each) and then stopped uploading sat flat at about 460K subscribers with roughly 1,000 views a day in mid 2025, showing that 3D polish alone does not keep a channel alive without a regular release rhythm.

Boey Bear's most viewed videos are practical toddler moments (hide and seek with toys 2.13M, a pretend dentist visit 2.05M, an ABC phonics video 1.38M, cars 1.34M, learn to talk 1.22M), the same routine and first experience topics that power the big channels.

On vidIQ's all time most viewed list (17 Nov 2026) about 13 of the top 40 channels are kids or family channels: CoComelon is second overall (about 230B views), followed by Kids Diana Show (126.8B), Vlad and Niki (124.3B), Like Nastya (123.8B) and Toys and Colors (123.4B), so kids content is roughly a third of YouTube's all time giants.

Only three pure song brands are in that all time top 40 (CoComelon, El Reino Infantil 76.3B and Super Simple Songs 65.1B, plus Plim Plim 62.4B as a song and show hybrid), while newer family Shorts channels (an Indian child Shorts channel at 124.9B, Sierra and Rhia 108.8B, Cadel and Mia 83.8B, J House jr. 63.4B) climbed past most of them in a few years on Shorts volume.

Kidshire (channel country UAE, started 7 Nov 2024) reached about 6.21M subscribers and 15.6B views from only about 160 videos by 17 Nov 2026, drawing about 545M views in 28 days on roughly two uploads a week, almost all from simple picture word Shorts, the clearest proof that a handful of very strong kids Shorts can carry a new channel.

Kidshire's subscriber growth peaked at about 760K in November 2025 (its first winter, when the winter clothes Short took off) and was still about 190K in October 2026, so one seasonal hit Short can lift a channel for a whole year.

Toys and Colors' separate Shorts channel (4.7M subscribers, about 1,170 videos) went from about 3 to 6M daily views in late March 2025 to 10 to 19M a day in April (about 357M in 28 days) while posting only about once a week, showing that Shorts channels grow in sudden jumps when one clip catches, not in steady steps.

The Singing Walrus (Canada, English songs for kids) has about 4.01M subscribers and 2.67B views and still gained about 26.5M views and 40K subscribers in the 28 days to 17 Nov 2026 without uploading since 3 Oct, so a catalogue of evergreen classroom songs keeps earning for weeks when uploads pause.

The Singing Walrus's top videos are an ABC phonics song (about 26M views, posted Apr 2025), a feelings and emotions song (15M) and a counting by 2s song (5.8M), and its holiday songs (Christmas 3.1M, Halloween 2.5M) come back each season through long compilations, so phonics, feelings and skip counting are proven English learning topics worth a Bro Bros version.

Dream English Kids is run by one named ESL teacher, Matt, who has made vocabulary songs since 2008 for ages 2 to 5 with clear, repeated target words; English learning guides recommend it over bigger brands precisely because it is one real teacher with a steady voice, which is the trust signal a channel with fixed brother voices can also offer.

In ChannelCrawler's list of the fastest growing US education channels for May 2026, three of the top 10 were kids channels: CoComelon (+1M subscribers in 30 days), Twin Twin, where identical twin sisters pair short stories with simple life lessons (+650K, up about 19% in a month), and SparkleToon, which teaches crafts and good manners in long videos and Shorts (+400K, up about 11%).

Twin Twin went from a fast growing US education channel in May 2026 (+650K subscribers in a month) to Tubefilter's worldwide most viewed top 50 by mid November (about 331M weekly views) in about six months, a recent case of a duo format with a small lesson in every video scaling very quickly.

Malaysia's Upin and Ipin (Les' Copaque, about 26.5M subscribers and 17.4B views) still earned about 123M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 with no net subscriber growth, and its five most viewed uploads (100M to 139M each) are full episodes about everyday values and a festive song episode for Hari Raya, so a beloved twin pair plus long story episodes keeps a mature channel earning from its back catalogue.

Little Buddy Kids (US, about 514K subscribers) drew about 96M views and 39K subscribers in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 with only 5 uploads, yet its most viewed long video has under 700K views, so nearly all of that reach comes from Shorts of classic songs and alphabet animals; a small song channel can reach 3M views a day through Shorts while its long videos stay small.

Robocar POLI's English song channel (about 893K subscribers and 690M views) gets only about 8M views a month despite the brand's TV fame and about three uploads a week, and its newest Shorts start with a few thousand views, so a famous character does not by itself make songs grow on YouTube; its top videos are 10 minute compilations (summer song 20.8M, car and school bus safety songs 19.8M).

Robocar POLI's 'It's Okay to Make Mistakes' good habits song has about 19M views (2022) and a later good habits compilation built around it about 12M, so a cheerful 'oops, that's okay, try again' song is a proven global theme worth a Bro Bros version, and it matches the 'resilience' word children chose in Oxford's survey.

Sunny Kids Songs (Australia, 2.89M subscribers, 2.17B views, best video a dentist check up song at 121M) fell from about 50M views a month in July 2024 to about 7M in October 2026 and gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 12 Nov 2026, with no upload since May 2026, so a toddler song channel that stops publishing can lose most of its monthly views within about two years.

Kids Funny Songs' 16 Nov 2026 upload, a 'this is the way we brush our teeth' morning routine song, drew about 93K views in its first 36 hours, faster than its bike riding (63K in 2.5 days) and egg reveal (55K in 1.5 days) songs that week, so daily routine songs remain the quickest starters on a big toddler channel.

Scratch Garden (Canada, about 2.34M subscribers, up from 984K in Nov 2023) gains about 30 to 40K subscribers and about 30M views a month with only about six uploads a month; its biggest videos are 'The Floor is Lava!' (35.6M) and numbered freeze dance songs (Dance Freeze Song 5, 31.5M; Dance Freeze Song 4, a clean up version, 30M), so numbered sequels of a movement game, even themed to chores, keep paying off.

India's Kids TV (about 31M subscribers, 16.7B views) has had flat subscribers since about October 2025 but still draws 36M to 74M views a month, with its best month in January 2026 (about 74M) and its lowest in October 2026, another sign that toddler song viewing peaks in the winter holiday months and that view totals matter more than subscriber growth for a mature song library.

Moja Magic TV (Nigeria), a small English kids channel making ABC, phonics, animal sounds and fruit songs, posted about 50 videos in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 (near our two a day pace), gained about 21K subscribers to reach 38.6K and drew about 46.5M views, while its best long videos have only 5K to 22K views, so a brand new song channel's breakout can come almost entirely from Shorts within a month.

HooplaKidz (US, about 11.6M subscribers, 6.9B views) gained no subscribers in September or October 2026 yet still added about 53M to 96M views a month from July to October; its top videos are finger family songs (533M and 264M), a 'Zooby zombie family sleeping in the bed' song (210M) and five dancing skeletons on the bus (188M), so gentle, silly monster versions of classic counting songs remain huge.

HooplaKidz's separate Hoopla Halloween channel (about 1.9M subscribers, 1.08B views) gains roughly 10M to 18M views in every month of the year, with October 2026 (about 10M) not even its best month and April 2026 its strongest, and its biggest videos are cute skeleton colour and finger family songs (100M to 139M), so friendly skeleton and monster songs are an all year topic for toddlers, not only a Halloween one.

Radio Flyer's toy brand series Max and Maple (season 2 on YouTube from 2 Nov 2026, ages 4 to 7) drops one 7 minute episode every three weeks, each with an original song, and fills the gaps with spin off Shorts, music videos, character Shorts and a podcast on the same channel, a slow hero episode plus fast filler rhythm.

Max and Maple pairs a dog and a beaver with a magic red wagon and builds every story on outdoor active play and problem solving, showing that brand funded kids shows on YouTube now sell 'safe, positive, active' as their main promise to parents.

Pinkfong's Baby Shark 'sound play' musical in Seoul (2 Dec 2026 to 28 Mar 2027) has no seats: families walk through seven zones on missions, sing parts of the songs themselves with light up microphones, and meet new triplet younger siblings, showing that new little sibling characters keep a long running brand fresh.

In Tubefilter's top 50 for the week to 15 Nov 2026 the biggest percentage jumps were Shorts channels built on curiosity and games (a Roblox Shorts channel up about 4,200% and an Indian 'experiments' Shorts channel up about 4,600%), while the only clear family channel, Like Nastya, held a steady 1M a week at 134M subscribers.

The same chart shows sensational Shorts spikes fading fast: Sasha Show fell 14% week on week and Leo Show about 50% after their October surges, while steady family brands kept flat gains, which supports building Bro Bros on consistent original songs rather than chasing shock style Shorts.

The official Mister Rogers' Neighborhood YouTube channel had 8.66M views from just 10 episodes by Sep 2026, and about 28% came through the YouTube Kids app, so for gentle preschool content the Kids app is a large, separate door worth designing for (clean thumbnails and titles that pass its filters).

GoNoodle reaches about 19.5M kids a year mostly through classrooms, yet its YouTube channel grew only about 20K followers in the year to Sep 2026 (about 1.73M) while posting about five times a week; its 'Back in Motion' back to school dance workout drew about 1.4M views in a month against 34K to 87K for other new uploads.

GoNoodle's 2026 slate leans on licensed partners (Star Wars movement and mindfulness, a Dr. Seuss literacy channel, a Great Wolf Lodge mascot video) plus social emotional series, so its YouTube peaks come from school calendar moments; an original 'back to school after the winter break' dance song for early January is the matching Bro Bros move.

Koo Koo Kanga Roo (two adult performers, weekly uploads, about 100K+ subscribers) wins with goofy one topic songs (a dinosaur stomp, pizza, a roller coaster) shown with colourful graphics and on screen lyrics, but a family review (Apr 2026) warned parents about toilet humour and one political song, a reminder to keep Bro Bros free of politics and gross out edges.

CoComelon's first brand campaign ('CoComelon Can Help', Apr 2025) sold its songs as help for parents with three hard routines (potty training, bedtime and mealtime), backed by its routine hits (Bath Song about 7B views, Yes Yes Vegetables 3.3B, Yes Yes Bedtime 1.7B, Potty Training 420M+), and pushed playlists by age and stage on Pinterest, Babylist and music apps.

That campaign also used parent creators on TikTok for candid, funny parenting confessions rather than kid facing ads, so Bro Bros Reels aimed at parents (a 'this song got my toddler to brush' style caption) can sit beside the kid facing dance Reels.

Morphle TV kept sliding: about 8.7M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 (down from about 15M a month in October) despite 23 new uploads, and its 17 Nov 'Morphle vs. T-Rex time machine rescue' episode had only about 3K views after a day and a half, so posting almost daily cannot revive a tired 3D cartoon brand without a fresh hook.

Morphle's newest titles still stack two kid magnets (a dinosaur plus a rescue or time machine) yet barely move, while its all time hits are emotion and transformation moments from 2022, a sign that title keywords alone stopped working for big legacy channels and new characters or formats are what audiences respond to now.

Pinkfong's company wide totals in Nov 2026 are about 250B YouTube views and about 320M subscribers across its channels, from over 8,800 pieces of content in 25 languages, plus 200 app series downloaded over 530M times; scale came from re versioning one song library into many languages and formats, not from ever more new songs.

Super Simple Songs' 2026 breakout list includes 'I'm a Baby Fish', a sing along with its new Finny Babies characters (about 13M views in four months, 1.9x its median), so even the category leader keeps launching new baby character sub brands inside its main channel; a Bro Bros 'baby animal friends' mini cast could do the same.

Little Baby Songs still shows 1.02M subscribers but gained only about 5K to 9K views a month through 2026 (about 230 a day), with its newest upload at 725 views after four months and its 'best' recent items being remixes and live compilations, a warning that a big subscriber count is worthless once a kids channel stops releasing fresh, recommendable originals.

Super Simple Play with Caitie posted 'Let's visit a Winter Village!' on 17 Nov 2026 and it ran at about 2x the channel's usual pace in its first day and a half (about 28K views, 280 views an hour), a fresh sign that Christmas themed uploads already outperform in the third week of November.

Nursery Rhyme Street (1.96M subscribers, about 35 uploads in the last 28 days, many of them remixes) had its strongest 2026 month in October with about 19M views, nearly double its usual 7M to 13M, and a 'spooky pizza party with skeletons' song uploaded in May 2026 already has about 14M views, so a friendly food plus skeleton mash up song can be a hit even outside Halloween.

RhymeMusicBox, a 44 video remix channel tied to a bigger nursery brand, got almost all its 178M views from two medley videos (about 128M and 21M) and stopped growing after uploads ended in October 2024, showing that a medley of two famous songs can explode once, but without steady new uploads the channel flattens.

Tubefilter's chart for the week of 15 Nov 2026 says Argentina's preschool clown cartoon El Payaso Plim Plim has not had a single week under 250M views in the past six months, proof that one gentle, kid friendly character brand can hold a huge steady audience week after week.

Blippi posted every day from 8 to 17 Nov 2026 (median gap one day since 1 Oct), mostly 25 to 56 second Shorts plus a 30 minute episode and a 2 hour vehicle race compilation; its strongest new Shorts were a Magnatile build in 45 seconds challenge (about 209K), counting by popping a fidget toy (29 seconds, about 183K) and 'what would Blippi look like as an animal' (about 157K).

An emotions Short where Blippi turns his frown upside down (13 Nov 2026, 50 seconds, about 141K views) did as well as his challenge Shorts, and none of his ten newest uploads up to 17 Nov were Christmas themed, so big preschool brands still hold holiday content until late November.

Pinkfong is turning December into a physical touchpoint in Japan (Christmas pop up shops in Tokyo on 4 Dec and Osaka on 11 Dec with about 50 new products including Bebefinn sibling dolls), and its Bebefinn music pad hit No. 1 in Amazon Japan music toys, showing that a sibling trio of characters is what it now sells hardest; our two brothers are a similar sibling hook.

Super Simple Songs turned 20 in 2026 (YouTube blog, Aug 2026): Skyship now has over 70M subscribers and about 90B views across its channels, and marked the date with a new celebration song, a studio tour led by its on screen host, a limited vinyl album and an in app kids experience, turning a channel milestone into several pieces of content.

Super Simple's chief executive says the company still works from its founding purpose, teachers writing simple songs to help children learn English, a reminder that a clear learning purpose is what made the brand last 20 years.

Pinkfong's Bebefinn Mother Goose music pad went straight to No. 1 on Amazon Japan in music toys and keyboard instruments in Nov 2026 and a Baby Shark alphabet bus leads English learning toys on Rakuten, so in Japan the songs sell as English learning tools.

Pinkfong is also opening Japan's first Baby Shark themed family hotel rooms at a hot spring resort near Tokyo and Bebefinn Christmas pop up shops in Tokyo (4 Dec) and Osaka (11 Dec) with about 50 new products, showing how a kids song brand grows into physical places once its characters are loved.
CoComelon: The Movie was first announced for 26 Feb 2027 (Nov 2025) and later given a 19 Feb 2027 date in Moonbug's first look (May 2026), so the 19 Feb date in the tree is the current one.

Ozzy Fox, the music led preschool short form series Animaj co produces with Disney Jr., passed 30M YouTube views in four months since its July 2026 launch, averages over 1.4M views per episode in the first 30 days, and arrives on Disney+ on 5 Dec 2026 with season 2 already greenlit, proof that a song per episode YouTube series can graduate to a streamer.

Dave and Ava's views are still growing even with flat subscribers: October 2026 brought about 46.9M views against 38.8M in October 2025 (about 21% more) while it uploads about five videos a week, so a big back catalogue plus steady uploads keeps a 3D nursery channel rising through search and suggested views.

Dave and Ava's newest upload (16 Nov 2026) is a sequel title, 'The Wheels on the Bus Part 2', reusing its best known song with a new animal theme; it had about 17K views in its first day and a half, a sign that 'Part 2' versions of a proven song are a cheap way to reuse a winning search title.

Mother Goose Club is shrinking while uploading only about 1.5 videos a week: October 2026 views were about 21M, roughly 38% below October 2025, and its 12 Nov Thanksgiving greeting had only about 20K views after five days; low upload frequency plus live action nursery content is losing ground to animated channels.

As of 18 Nov 2026 neither Dave and Ava nor Mother Goose Club had a new Christmas video among their recent uploads, so in mid November the Christmas search space is still open for a fresh Bro Bros Christmas song uploaded now.

FunForKidsTV (3.12M subscribers, 2.37B views from only 352 videos) still gains about 20K subscribers and 37.6M views a month with just 9 uploads in 28 days; its all time top videos are 2023 story remixes of a famous song with a small problem in the title (a 'got a boo boo' version reached about 142M views).

FunForKidsTV's newest Short (14 Nov 2026) is a guessing game, 'Can You Guess Which Shape Is the Best Dancer?', with about 26K views in four days; a 'guess which one dances best' question in the title turns a dance Short into a game children answer out loud, a shape Bro Bros can use with our own characters.

FunForKidsTV's monthly views peaked at about 78M in August 2026 and fell to about 34M by October, while it had no Christmas video by 18 Nov; mid size nursery channels that skip the seasonal wave drift down in autumn, so seasonal songs are part of keeping views up through Q4.

Even the biggest rival can disappear overnight: a 22M subscriber kids channel that grew by imitating CoComelon lost everything to copyright strikes, which shows that in kids animation scale built on copying is fragile and original characters are the only durable asset.

Lalafun Kids Songs US (3.39M subscribers, 1.87B views, 3,456 videos since Mar 2022) drew about 17M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 from 11 new uploads, with zero net new subscribers; a year earlier it was getting about 53M views and 40K subscribers a month.

That feed's biggest videos are long compilations led by a baby animals bus song (about 413M views, Apr 2024) and a colours ducks song (176M, Dec 2024), while its newest original song (18 Nov 2026, a 'what should I eat?' food choice song) had about 1.6K views after 17 hours, so for mass upload channels old compilations carry the views and new singles add little.

Lalafun's high volume model (thousands of similar videos spread over several sister feeds) is losing reach in 2026: the US feed is down about two thirds year on year and the Canada feed even lost views in Oct 2026, which suggests volume alone no longer works and fits YouTube's push against repetitive, mass produced kids content.

Mediawan's kids and family president (Jan 2026) expects digital first animation, a strong return of action adventure and targeted live action to lead in 2026, notes a Miraculous chibi series launched on Roblox before YouTube, and warns AI will bring 'a tsunami' of user made kids content that makes a clear brand and characters the main way to stand out.

Hogi's newest Short (17 Nov 2026), 'Toot! Toot! Let's Play Party Horn', reached about 60K views in its first 11 hours, so Pinkfong is already seeding New Year party sounds six weeks ahead; a noisy party toy (horn, popper, drum) as the hook object is the kind of sound kids repeat.

With the same pace of about five uploads a week, Hogi (Shorts plus toy object songs) gained about 100K subscribers in 28 days and about 217M views, while Dave and Ava (long classic nursery rhymes) gained none and about 46M views; its 18 Nov 'Row Row Row Your Boat' had about 9K views in 10 hours at 0.8% engagement.

Super Supremes (4M subscribers, flat all year) posted its first Christmas Short on 17 Nov 2026 titled 'Jingle Bell' followed by hashtags like #viral #trending #popular #xmas, and it reached only about 940 views in 36 hours, more proof that stuffing generic hashtags into titles does nothing without a strong first frame.

Super Supremes' two most viewed videos ever are Halloween songs from Oct 2021 and Oct 2022 (about 10.1M and 9.1M) ahead of its 'Wheels on the Bus' (9.1M), matching Dave and Ava, where Halloween also tops the list, so for US rhyme channels the holiday songs become the long term top earners.

Plim Plim's English channel (2.04M subscribers, 1.14B views, checked 17 Nov 2026) uploaded about 48 times from 30 Aug to 15 Nov (30 long videos, 18 Shorts), roughly 4 to 5 a week, mixing 1 to 2 hour themed compilations (vehicles, dinosaurs, kindness) with 1 minute emoji titled Shorts tagged #shortskids.

Plim Plim's 2 minute 'Kindness is My Superpower' song, posted 2 Nov 2026 after three 'something special is coming' teaser Shorts and timed to World Kindness Day (13 Nov), reached about 1.1M views in 15 days while its other November uploads sat at 11K to 98K, so a short single with a feelings theme, teased by Shorts, can be a channel's breakout of the month.

Plim Plim's biggest recent Short was a 'scared to jump in the water' moment (3.1M views, Sep 2026) and its best long video a freeze dance (1.3M, Oct), and in October about 8 Halloween uploads led the channel (a peek a boo song 530K, a potion colour mixing song 454K), confirming that small fears overcome, freeze games and seasonal colour songs are the top performers for this kind of channel.

A US nursery rhyme channel with 1.02M subscribers (Little Baby Songs) has posted nothing since 10 Jul 2026, gains no subscribers and now gets only about 130 to 480 views a day, so subscriber count alone keeps no channel alive without steady uploads.

Bebefinn's newest upload (18 Nov 2026) is an emotions song built as a question plus a lesson ('Why are you crying? Use your words!') and passed about 196K views in its first 13 hours, faster than its ballet and car mechanic songs, so naming a feeling and teaching what to say instead is a strong current preschool theme.

Lalafun's newest video (17 Nov 2026) is another 'Animal Version' of a classic rhyme, but it drew only about 44K views in its first 39 hours on a 15.3M subscriber channel, while the brand's mission and rescue titles start far faster, so the plain animal remix formula looks tired.

In the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 Lalafun (13 uploads) gained about 500K subscribers and 555M views while Bebefinn (20 uploads) gained about 300K and 399M, so fewer, stronger long songs beat higher volume for subscriber growth.

As of 18 to 19 Nov 2026 neither Lalafun nor Bebefinn main English channels had a Christmas themed upload among their newest videos, confirming that the top 3D song brands open their Christmas push only in the last week of November or later.

In the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 Little Angel's main channel posted 28 videos, about one a day, and its views rose 21% against the previous two weeks (about 1.1M a day), so a steady daily rhythm with Shorts mixed in is lifting an old nursery brand.

In the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026 ChuChu TV posted only 9 uploads, all long story or learning compilations, and its views fell 22% against the prior two weeks (about 8M a day from the back catalogue), so slow long only uploading is not reviving a giant channel.

Little Angel's 'Can You Count with Firefighter Jill?' Short (15 Nov 2026) scored about 2.1 times the channel's usual views with only 0.8% engagement, showing that a helper job character plus a 'can you' question works even when few viewers like or comment, typical of made for kids audiences.

Super Simple Songs posted only 3 videos in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 yet gained about 200K subscribers (100K in the last week) and drew about 17.6M views a day, while Little Angel posted 28 videos and gained only about 10K, so for big brands a few carefully made, trusted songs beat daily volume.

Super Simple's silly worded hand and face washing song (5 Nov 2026) kept climbing to about 1.86M views in two weeks, about 3 times the channel's usual pace and its best recent upload, so a playful nonsense word hook on an everyday care routine is this autumn's strongest preschool song pattern.

Bebefinn's newest episode (18 Nov 2026), 'Why Are You Crying, Finn? Don't Cry, Use Your Words!', drew about 196K views in its first 13 hours, faster than its ballet song the week before (about 247K in a day and a half), so a feelings song where a little one learns to say what is wrong instead of crying is a proven fast starter; our 'Use Your Words!' idea should be made next week.

Little Angel's newest dubbed uploads (17 and 18 Nov 2026) open with fewer than 10K views in their first day or two even on 5M to 17M subscriber channels (a dinosaur animal dance party in Indonesian 9.7K, a wheels on the train song in Arabic 4.3K, a Bingo 'who was in our house?' mess mystery in Portuguese 9K), showing that subscriber count no longer pushes new videos and each upload must earn its own clicks.

Cocobi's children's song about chocolate causing tooth cavities (Jan 2026) is about the 13th most viewed Short of 2026 at roughly 926M views, a second proof after VocaVoca that a short healthy habit song with a food or tooth hook travels worldwide.

vidIQ's fastest growing list (updated 19 Nov 2026) has only one pure kids song channel in its top 50, VocaVoca at No. 48 with about 1.1M new subscribers in 30 days (11.1M total, about 16.2B lifetime views), next to the brand channel Pokémon Kids TV at No. 20 (about 1.7M gained).

Jugnu Kids, a Hindi nursery rhyme channel with 17.6M subscribers and over 5,300 videos, still drew about 34M views in 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 from 22 uploads but gained zero subscribers, and its newest classic rhyme cartoon had under 9K views after 13 hours, showing how old catalogues keep views while new uploads stop growing the channel.

A US channel named BabyFun Kids Songs shows about 452K subscribers but only about 640K lifetime views, 18 videos and about 1.8K views in 28 days, so a kids channel's subscriber count alone says nothing; Bro Bros should judge rivals and itself by recent views per upload.

Kids TV Español Latino (Mexico, about 6.3M subscribers, 2.57B lifetime views) drew about 19M views and 10K new subscribers in the 28 days to 20 Nov 2026 from 14 uploads, and its new Christmas bells song (17 Nov) had only about 1.3K views after three days, showing that a big Spanish catalogue does not lift a brand new seasonal upload by itself.

Lalafun drew about 555M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 against about 702M in October, while still adding about 500K subscribers in 28 days (200K in the last week) from 13 uploads, so even top kids song channels see a November dip between the Halloween peak and the Christmas lift.

In Metricool's 2026 YouTube study only 11% of accounts under 10,000 subscribers moved up a size tier between Feb 2025 and Feb 2026, so growing past 10K is rare and Bro Bros should judge progress by views per upload and returning viewers, not by expecting quick subscriber jumps.

Christian kids streamer Minno (1.7M YouTube subscribers, over 200M views in a year) signed Bible song animation channel Listener Kids on 19 Nov 2026 to a worldwide multi year deal: 66 new episodes premiere on Minno first and reach YouTube later, and Minno says more YouTube Kids creator deals are coming before the end of 2026.

NuNu Tv Nursery Rhymes holds the most viewed YouTube Short of all time on Viralteca's weekly re ranked list (a 'One Two Three' number song, about 5.7B views) and three more of its Shorts entered the top 100 this week ('Rabbit Went Over the Mountain' 2.2B, 'Ten Little Buses' 1.7B, 'Ten Little Airplanes' 868M), so 'ten little' counting songs with vehicles keep scaling.

CoComelon's animal spin off channel Stay Paw-sitive (created Nov 2022, 2.91M subscribers, about 1.8B views) published 19 videos in the 28 days to 20 Nov 2026 for about 22.4M views, and its monthly views swing between about 17M and 32M (Oct 2026 was 32.1M), mostly from remixed classic songs.

Stay Paw-sitive's newest upload on 17 Nov 2026 is a vacuum cleaner rescue song with the animal characters, so a household helper machine is a live topic for big brands right now, matching our Vroom Vroom Vacuum song idea.

CoComelon runs a separate loops channel that stretches one song (Rocketship, Finger Family, Bingo) into 30 minute and 1 hour loops (252 videos, about 974K subscribers and roughly 10M views a month in mid 2025), showing a single hit song can be repackaged as a long loop video for background listening.

Peppa Pig and Sesame Street released their first crossover on 2 Sep 2026, a 1.5 minute 'Muddy Puddles' dance remix that mashes each brand's own puddle jumping song, posted on both YouTube channels, so big kids brands now grow by remixing a shared everyday theme into an upbeat dance track.

Hasbro made Peppa Pig's first special aimed at parents (premiered 11 Aug 2026 on a podcast's YouTube channel, about parenthood and self care), showing kids brands now court the parent who picks the video as well as the child.

Spain's Cleo and Cuquin was relaunched with YouTube exclusive content and that digital comeback led HBO Max to commission a second Cuquin season, more proof that a strong YouTube kids brand can later be sold to streamers.

Super Simple Songs released its 2026 original songs on a strict every other Thursday rhythm (19 songs from 8 Jan to 24 Sep, every one on a Thursday), so even a top channel builds its catalogue with a steady fixed day rather than a flood of uploads.

Those 2026 Super Simple originals run only 2 to 4 minutes and use plain titles that name one loved thing or one skill ('I Love My Pet', 'Put on your Shoes', 'Our Listening Ears', 'Counting up to 20'), with just one compilation (a lullaby medley) in nine months.

BabyBus's strongest November 2026 uploads turn a tiny everyday problem into a song: 'My Zipper's Stuck!' (set to a 'this is the way' tune) reached about 1.36M views in two weeks and 'My Nose Is Growing' (don't lie) about 611K, while a plain brush your teeth remake got 194K, so a stuck or silly moment in the title beats a plain routine.

BabyBus (44.2M subscribers) posted about 27 to 36 long videos a month through 2026 and zero Shorts, gaining about 178M views and 100K subscribers in 28 days, and as of 20 Nov 2026 had no Christmas title among its newest uploads; its biggest Christmas video (a traffic jam on Christmas Eve song, 57M) is eight years old and keeps working.
A 'Wheels on the race car' version that teaches shapes drew about 1.12M views in nine days on BabyBus, another sign that a vehicle twist plus one learning concept is a reliable title formula.

BabyBus's spin off Sheriff Labrador (10.9M subscribers) kept adding about 100K subscribers a month in Jul to Nov 2026 with safety and sharing cartoons; its 13 Nov episode 'The Mud Ball Mystery' got about 424K views in 2.5 days, showing a single recurring hero with a lesson in every title builds a second channel fast.

In the global list of fastest growing YouTube channels for 13 to 20 Nov 2026 the only kids song channels are LooLoo Kids (+100K subscribers, about 168M weekly views, 62.8M total) and Super Simple Songs (+100K, about 119M views, 47.3M total), while family vlog style Like Nastya added about 1M, so classic English sing along channels grow steadily but slowly at the top.

CoComelon gained about 344M views in the same seven days, more than twice LooLoo Kids and almost three times Super Simple Songs, so it still takes the lion's share of English preschool song viewing in late November.

CoComelon posted about 12 to 14 long videos and 16 to 24 Shorts every month of 2026 (about 153 long and 218 Shorts in 12 months) and gained about 1.06B views in 28 days to 20 Nov, so even the biggest kids channel runs on a steady weekly rhythm of roughly three long videos and four Shorts.

CoComelon's strongest November 2026 long videos are everyday family songs: 'Cooking Dinner Song, Making a Mess with JJ' reached about 1.96M views in three days and an indoor playground peekaboo song about 1.67M, ahead of its winter ski race (1.32M) and a grandparents train song (429K in a day), so messy, playful home routines remain the safest lead songs even in holiday season.

In mid November CoComelon puts winter mostly into Shorts (build a snowman while counting blocks, count the arctic animals, a festive Santa craft) and saves long form for core songs, a cheap way to test seasonal themes before committing a full Christmas song.

Danny Go!, started in 2019 by a husband, wife and two childhood friends, had over 4.5M subscribers, nearly 5B lifetime views and 65 sold out live shows by spring 2026, then added a Netflix series (from April) and a picture book (31 Mar 2026), showing the path from a small team movement channel to TV, stage and books once songs become a recognisable brand.

Junior Squad (5.45M subscribers) switched to Christmas from 5 Nov 2026, but its Christmas long videos drew only about 700 to 3,300 views each by 19 Nov while its 54 second Santa finger family Short reached about 17.5K, and the channel lost about 10K subscribers in 28 days, so an early Christmas push does not rescue a fading channel and Shorts carry the early seasonal test better than long videos.

Blippi's holiday flavoured 'Great Bake Off, paint a Blippi on a pie' Short (17 Nov 2026, 44 s) had about 14K views after a day or two while his fidget toy popping and counting Short (15 Nov, 29 s) passed 183K, so a sensory learning hook still beats a seasonal cooking theme in mid November.

After its 'Kindness Is My Superpower' song passed about 1.1M views, Plim Plim's English channel (2.04M subscribers) followed with kindness and sharing compilations and a sharing song (7 to 15 Nov 2026) that drew only about 11K to 43K views each, so one hit does not carry its follow ups; a hit should get its own Short cuts and sequels with a new hook, not just repackaged compilations right away.

ChuChuTV Hindi (16.8M subscribers) lost about 100K subscribers in the 28 days to 11 Nov 2026 on about 29M views, and its newest upload, a Diwali song collection in 4K (1 Nov), had only about 55K views after nine days, so even a festival song from the biggest Indian rhyme brand barely moves when it is a repackaged collection rather than one new song.

ChuChu TV's Surprise Eggs learning channel (9.33M subscribers) posted nothing between 3 Oct and 9 Nov 2026 yet still gained about 10K subscribers on about 25M views in 28 days, and its last upload (a banana song with surprise eggs) passed 500K views in five weeks, so a toy reveal plus song format keeps earning from the back catalogue long after uploads stop.

Bebefinn's English main channel drew about 664M views and 500K new subscribers in December 2025, against about 399M views and 300K subscribers in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026, so even a mature 3D song brand gets roughly a 60% December lift; our Christmas and winter songs should be live by the first days of December to ride it.

Bebefinn's Traditional Chinese channel (1.83M subscribers, about 19 uploads in four weeks) got its best recent views from a 'bath time pirates' Short (about 368K) and colour play songs (about 194K to 214K), while its hour long Halloween compilation drew about 47K, so in Taiwan and Hong Kong short pretend play routine clips beat long seasonal compilations.

In a third party chart of 2026's 100 most viewed long videos (as of 20 Nov), the kids entries (LooLoo Kids three times, BabyBus, Super Simple Songs, Toddler Zoo, Vlad and Niki) are all learning songs or toy stories from dedicated kids channels whose titles state the lesson (colours, sharing, animal sounds), so each Bro Bros title should name one clear learning hook.

Only one kids video (LooLoo Kids' colours and marble run nursery rhyme, about 467M) sits in the top 30 most viewed long videos of 2026 next to music stars and MrBeast, so the biggest kids hits of the year still come from a toy or object hook (balls, marble run) wrapped around a classic rhyme structure.

Moonbug's Little Bus Kids Songs channel (2.18M subscribers, about 893M views, 2,021 videos) still uploads about 3 times a week but has gained no subscribers since April 2026 and runs at only 2 to 4M views a month, a warning that a channel built on reposted clips from other brands stalls, while original characters keep growing.
